Name: Enoshima Island
Description: Shrines, sea caves, island streets. Try tako senbei (pressed octopus cracker) and matcha sweets.
Best Time To Visit: ~11:45am-12:45pm - time for the shrines and the top of the island, not the sea caves. Then the Enoden to Kamakura (about 25 min)

Name: Shirakawa-go
Description: UNESCO World Heritage mountain village famous for traditional gassho-zukuri farmhouses with steep thatched roofs.
Best Time To Visit: January-February (snow) / October-November (autumn) | Best time of day: morning-afternoon
Reservation Info: No reservation needed for the village itself - some houses/museums inside may require a small admission fee, paid on site.

Name: Hase-dera
Description: Gardens, ocean views, and a 9.18m gilded wooden Kannon statue. 5 min walk from Kōtoku-in.

Name: Kamakura Daibutsu (Great Buddha of Kamakura)
Description: One of Japan's most famous Buddhist statues, a monumental bronze Buddha dating back to the 13th century.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:10-3:35pm: Enoden from Kamakura to Hase (5 min) after lunch, then a 10 min walk. Back at Kamakura Station by ~3:55pm

Name: Kamakura Station restrooms
Description: Free, reliable restrooms right at the station before or after the Enoden line to Hase.

Name: Tsubame Cafe
Description: Teishoku (set meal) lunch in a beautifully curated old Japanese house near the station. ORDER: the curry set (highly praised, comes with rice and a small side) or the medicinal curry plate — both come with a tofu dessert finish. Popular enough that showing up right at opening is recommended, or book via their Instagram.
Best Time To Visit: Right at opening
Reservation Info: Arrive at opening, or book via Instagram

Name: 21st Century Museum of Contemporary Art restrooms
Description: The museum's free public zone (no ticket needed) includes clean restrooms — convenient midpoint between Nagamachi and the Higashi Chaya district.

Name: Antique & Vintage Shops Around Tatemachi Street
Description: Area with independent vintage clothing shops, antique stores, and small boutiques away from tourist crowds.
Best Time To Visit: March - May / September - November | Best time of day: 12:00-17:00

Name: Curio Espresso and Vintage Design Café
Description: Good espresso-and-sandwich break between Nagamachi and the museums. ORDER: the breakfast sandwich (fluffy eggs, ham, lettuce in an English muffin) with a latte — their signature combination.

Name: Fuwari
Neighborhood: Owaricho (3 min walk from Omicho Market)
Description: Well-regarded izakaya known for rare nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch) sushi at a notably fair price, with a complimentary otoshi appetizer on being seated. Traditional dishes come with an intentional modern twist. Good walk-in option if you haven't booked ahead for dinner.
Best Time To Visit: Early dinner (~17:00) to walk in without a wait
Must See Highlight: Order the nodoguro sushi if available that day
Reservation Info: Reservations by phone (050-3155-4540); walk-in possible if you arrive at the 17:00 opening

Name: Hakuichi Higashiyama Store
Description: One of Kanazawa's most famous gold leaf companies, showcasing the city's signature craft.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: afternoon

Name: Higashi Chaya District
Description: Kanazawa's most famous preserved geisha district, with Edo-period wooden tea houses, gold leaf shops, cafes and crafts.
Best Time To Visit: April-May / October-November | Best time of day: early morning / evening
Reservation Info: Free to walk around; individual tea houses/museums require tickets.

Name: Higashiyama Chaya District Cafés
Description: Traditional wooden tea houses converted into cafes, offering one of the best atmospheres in Kanazawa. ORDER: a matcha set with gold-leaf-topped sweets at whichever teahouse-cafe catches your eye. | Souvenir snack: Gold-leaf-topped sweets, a genuine Kanazawa specialty souvenir. [This is a district recommendation — several teahouse-cafes worth browsing within Higashi Chaya, not one single shop.]
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: afternoon
Reservation Info: Usually walk-in; some tea experiences require reservations.

Name: Iki-Iki Tei
Description: Casual seafood restaurant inside Omicho Market known for fresh seafood bowls and local fish. ORDER: the kaisendon (assorted sashimi rice bowl) featuring whatever's freshest that day. | Souvenir snack: None typical — sit-down restaurant.
Best Time To Visit: November - February
Reservation Info: Walk-ins accepted; arrive early to avoid lines.

Name: Iwamoto Kiyoshi Shouten
Description: Fifth-generation, 118-year-old artisan workshop hand-producing charred paulownia (kiri) wood trays and accessories
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Buy a small charred-paulownia tray or inlay piece — light, flat, and perfect for travel; ask to see the workshop and belt-driven machines

Name: Kaga Yuzen Traditional Industry Center
Description: Museum and workshop space dedicated to Kaga Yuzen silk dyeing, one of Kanazawa's most important traditional crafts.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: afternoon

Name: Kaikaro Teahouse
Description: Historic geisha teahouse where visitors can see traditional interiors and learn about geisha culture.
Best Time To Visit: ~2:00pm, first stop in Higashi Chaya after dropping bags (12:30pm arrival)
Reservation Info: Admission fee required; tea experiences may require reservation. Reserve tea experiences by phone or via the teahouse's website.

Name: Kaisen Ichiba (Omicho)
Description: Seafood bowls and grilled seafood, a step up from the market stalls. ORDER: the kaisendon or a grilled nodoguro set if available — Kanazawa's prized local fish. | Souvenir snack: Dried or vacuum-packed seafood.

Name: Kanazawa Castle Park
Description: Former headquarters of the powerful Maeda clan, whose Kaga domain made Kanazawa one of Edo Japan's wealthiest cities.
Best Time To Visit: April-May / October-November | Best time of day: 8:00-11:00
Reservation Info: Park is free; some restored buildings require admission.

Name: Kanazawa Kutani Ceramic Museum / Workshops
Description: Kutani porcelain is one of Ishikawa's most famous crafts, known for colorful hand-painted designs.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Kanazawa Station (Motenashi Dome / Tsuzumi-mon Gate)
Description: Free restrooms inside one of Japan's most photographed train stations — the wooden Tsuzumi-mon torii gate and glass dome are worth the stop even without needing the toilet.

Name: Kanazawa Station breakfast before Takayama departure
Description: Kanazawa Station has several bakeries and coffee shops in the Anto shopping area — good spot for a quick breakfast before picking up the rental car for the drive to Takayama. ORDER: whatever fresh-baked pastry looks good plus a coffee — this is a flexible grab-and-go stop, not a sit-down meal.
Best Time To Visit: Morning

Name: Kazuemachi Chaya District
Description: A smaller, quieter geisha district along the Asano River, known for atmospheric wooden buildings and fewer crowds than Higashi Chaya.
Best Time To Visit: April-May / October-November | Best time of day: sunset / evening

Name: Kenroku-en Garden
Description: One of Japan's three most beautiful landscape gardens, famous for seasonal scenery, ponds, streams, lanterns, and carefully designed views.
Best Time To Visit: ~2:30-3:45pm, after lunch at the station (bus to Kenrokuen-shita); garden open to 6pm through Oct 15

Name: Kenroku-en public restrooms (Renchi-mon Gate)
Description: Clean, free restrooms just inside the garden's main gate.

Name: Kintsuba Nakaya
Description: Traditional confectionery shop specializing in kintsuba, a simple but iconic Japanese red bean sweet. | Souvenir snack: Kintsuba (red bean sweets) — their namesake product, buy fresh, eat within a couple days.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: afternoon

Name: Korinbo Cafe Area
Description: The Korinbo area has many stylish cafes and is a convenient stop between sightseeing areas. ORDER: browse and pick whichever spot looks appealing — this is a district recommendation, not one shop. | Souvenir snack: Local roasted coffee beans if available.
Best Time To Visit: Quick coffee before the 8:00-9:00am car pickup - be on the road by ~9:00am

Name: Kourinbo Atrio / Department Store Food Floors
Description: Excellent place to buy regional sweets, local products, and beautifully packaged souvenirs. | Souvenir snack: Depachika-style boxed sweets and regional specialty snacks under one roof.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Mori Mori Sushi Kanazawa Forus
Description: One of Kanazawa's most popular conveyor-belt sushi restaurants, known for exceptional quality-to-price ratio using Sea of Japan seafood. ORDER: nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch) and kanpachi (amberjack) nigiri specifically — both genuine Hokuriku specialties worth seeking out here. | Souvenir snack: None typical — sit-down restaurant.
Best Time To Visit: November - February for peak seafood | Best time of day: lunch / dinner
Reservation Info: Usually no reservations; numbered ticket system during busy periods.

Name: Morihachi
Description: One of Kanazawa's oldest wagashi shops. Kintsuba (bean-filled, thin flour coating) and rakugan (dry sugar sweets). | Souvenir snack: Wagashi — one of Kanazawa's oldest confectioners (since 1625), a genuinely prestigious sweet souvenir.

Name: Myoryuji (Ninja Temple)
Description: A temple famous for hidden rooms, secret passages, traps, and unusual defensive architecture built during the Edo period.
Best Time To Visit: ~10:00-10:30am tour slot (book by phone), by bus from Omicho; then walk north through Tatemachi and Nagamachi
Reservation Info: Advance reservation required; tours are guided in Japanese with some multilingual support. Reserve by phone in advance (tours are conducted in Japanese); a travel agency or hotel concierge can help arrange an English-assisted visit.

Name: Nagamachi Samurai District
Description: A preserved samurai neighborhood where former warrior residences, earthen walls, canals, and traditional gardens showcase Edo-period life.
Best Time To Visit: April-May / October-November | Best time of day: morning / afternoon
Reservation Info: Free to walk around; museums require tickets.

Name: Nomura Samurai House
Description: Restored samurai residence showcasing the lifestyle of the wealthy warrior class during the Edo period.
Best Time To Visit: April-May / October-November | Best time of day: morning / afternoon

Name: Nouka Banzai The Shop Higashiyama
Description: Small well-curated shop selling local artisan crafts, lacquerware, ceramics, jewelry; supports Noto Peninsula artisans post-earthquake
Best Time To Visit: ~2:45pm, a few doors from Kaikaro - closes 5pm
Must See Highlight: Look for Kutani ware pieces and items made by Noto Peninsula artisans; ask staff about the story behind featured artists

Name: Ohi Pottery Museum & Kiln
Description: Ohi-yaki is Kanazawa's own 350-year-old raku-style pottery, developed for the local tea ceremony tradition. Small museum plus kiln viewing; quieter and less touristy than the gold leaf shops.

Name: Omicho Market
Description: Kanazawa's historic food market, operating for over 280 years and famous for seafood from the Sea of Japan. | Souvenir snack: Vacuum-packed local seafood, or dried goods from the stalls (avoid fresh seafood unless flying home same day).
Best Time To Visit: November - February (seafood season) | Best time of day: breakfast / lunch
Reservation Info: Free entry; restaurant reservations recommended for popular sushi counters. Reserve directly with individual sushi counters by phone; a hotel concierge can call on your behalf if needed.

Name: Oyama Shrine
Description: A unique shrine dedicated to Maeda Toshiie, founder of the Kaga domain, combining Japanese, Chinese, and Western architectural influences.
Best Time To Visit: March-May / October-November | Best time of day: morning

Name: Shiguretei Tea House (inside Kenroku-en)
Description: Matcha + wagashi set inside the garden. October sweets often feature chestnut, persimmon, maple motifs.

Name: Ekiben for the Kinosaki to Tokyo journey
Description: This is your longest travel day (~4-5hrs total via Kyoto/Shin-Osaka to Tokyo) — grab an ekiben at Kinosaki Station or during your transfer at Kyoto/Shin-Osaka Station for lunch on the way. San'in coast ekiben often feature local crab or seafood when in season.
Best Time To Visit: Before boarding, or during your transfer
Tags: ekiben; train bento; long travel day

Name: Kinosaki canal walk
Hours: Always open, best late afternoon and after dark
Description: Willow-lined canal, wooden ryokan, lanterns. Wear the yukata your ryokan provides and walk in geta.
Best Time To Visit: From ~2:00pm after the ~1:50pm arrival and dropping bags; best late afternoon and after dark

Name: Kinosaki Gelato Café Chaya
Description: Popular stop for handmade gelato while walking around the onsen town. | Souvenir snack: None (gelato doesn't travel) — enjoy on the spot.
Best Time To Visit: April - October | Best time of day: afternoon

Name: Kinosaki Mugiwara Zaiku Museum
Description: Museum showcasing Kinosaki's traditional straw craft, a unique local art form.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: afternoon

Name: Kinosaki Onsen Station restrooms
Description: Free restrooms at the station — most of the seven bathhouses also have their own changing-room restrooms once you're inside.

Name: Kinosaki Onsen Town Walk
Description: The main Kinosaki experience - strolling through a beautifully preserved hot spring town in a yukata, crossing stone bridges, and visiting bathhouses.
Best Time To Visit: November-March (crab season) / December-February (snow) / April-May | Best time of day: evening
Reservation Info: Free to explore; most ryokan guests receive a bathhouse pass included with their stay.

Name: Onsenji Temple
Description: Historic mountain temple connected to Kinosaki's onsen origins; traditionally visitors prayed here before bathing.
Best Time To Visit: April-May / October-November | Best time of day: morning / afternoon

Name: Sanpou Nishimuraya
Hours: Lunch and dinner vary by season
Description: A refined restaurant focused on Tajima regional cuisine, especially charcoal-grilled dishes, snow crab, and Tajima beef. | Souvenir snack: None typical — ryokan dinner.
Best Time To Visit: November - March | Best time of day: lunch / dinner
Reservation Info: Reservations recommended, especially during crab season. Reserve by phone directly with the restaurant, especially ahead of crab season.

Name: Seven Public Bathhouses (Sotoyu Meguri)
Description: The town's signature activity: visiting the seven historic public hot spring baths, each with its own character and design.
Best Time To Visit: November - March | Best time of day: evening / late night
Reservation Info: Ryokan guests typically receive a free pass; day visitors can purchase admission.

Name: % Arabica Arashiyama
Hours: Opens 9:00 on Mondays; no regular closed day (Tabelog, checked 16 Oct 2026)
Description: Famous coffee stop with a view of Togetsukyo Bridge. Kyoto latte or Spanish latte. | Souvenir snack: Bagged coffee beans.
Best Time To Visit: Optional - opens 9:00 on Mondays

Name: % Arabica Kyoto Higashiyama
Description: One of Kyoto's most famous coffee shops, located near Yasaka Pagoda with excellent views and specialty coffee. | Souvenir snack: Bagged coffee beans.
Best Time To Visit: ~10:35am coffee break - expect a queue

Name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
Description: One of Kyoto's most photographed natural landscapes, featuring towering bamboo paths near temples and gardens.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:45-8:40am, before the crowds

Name: Demachi Futaba
Description: Kyoto's most famous shop for fresh seasonal wagashi, especially the iconic mame daifuku.
Best Time To Visit: ~9:20am after breakfast - expect a line

Name: Demachi Masugata Market
Description: A genuine neighborhood market where Kyoto locals actually do their daily shopping — no stick-food stalls aimed at tourists, just produce vendors, small supermarkets, and century-old tea shops. Worth an early visit to catch the seafood arrival if you're up for it. A real contrast to Nishiki Market's tourist-facing stalls. | Souvenir snack: Loose-leaf tea from the century-old tea shops here.
Best Time To Visit: ~9:40-10:10am (some shops may still be opening). Leave by 10:10 to collect bags and be at Kyoto Station by 10:55 for the 11:25am Kinosaki train - buy an ekiben at the station for lunch
Must See Highlight: Go early to catch the daily rhythm of the market before tour groups are even awake

Name: Demachiyanagi Station restrooms
Description: Free restrooms at the station, right by Demachi Futaba if you're in line for mochi.

Name: Eikan-do Zenrin-ji
Description: One of Kyoto's most famous autumn foliage temples, featuring elegant gardens, ponds, and the unique "Looking Back Amida" Buddha statue.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - taken off Day 18 on 17 Oct 2026 - last entry is 4:00pm, which left no time for Ginkaku-ji before its 5:00pm close
Price: ¥1,000 (¥1,500 during the 11 Nov-6 Dec autumn exhibition)

Name: eXcafe Arashiyama
Description: Traditional machiya cafe where guests grill their own dango over charcoal in a beautiful Japanese setting. | Souvenir snack: Matcha sweets if sold at the counter.
Best Time To Visit: Optional - no time for a sit-down stop on the new Day 19 timeline
Reservation Info: Walk-ins; expect waits during peak seasons.

Name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
Description: Kyoto's most iconic shrine, famous for thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up Mount Inari, dedicated to the deity Inari.
Best Time To Visit: ~6:15-7:45am, the quietest time (sunrise 6:06). Leave your stay ~5:50: JR Nara Line from Kyoto Station to Inari, about 5 min. Then JR back to Kyoto Station for breakfast

Name: Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion)
Description: A Zen temple famous for understated beauty, moss gardens, sand gardens, and traditional aesthetics.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:20-4:00pm (closes 5:00pm), then a taxi to SOU・SOU

Name: Gion District
Description: Kyoto's most famous traditional entertainment district, known for wooden machiya houses, tea houses, restaurants, and geisha culture.

Name: Gion Shirakawa (bonus walk)
Description: A quieter stone-lantern canal walk near Pontocho — good add-on for your first Kyoto evening.

Name: Hannari Kyoto (はんなりKyoto) Ninenzaka
Hours: 10:00-18:00 daily, closed 1 Jan (official site, checked 18 Oct 2026)
Description: Gamaguchi (clasp-frame) specialist: wallets, coin purses and bags in traditional and modern Japanese fabric patterns - fabric, not leather. Replaced the 'Hannari Kyoto Leather Shop' entry on 18 Oct 2026: no leather shop of that name could be found, and the old pin and neighbourhood did not agree.
Best Time To Visit: ~10:25am on Ninen-zaka - opens 10:00

Name: Heian Shrine
Description: Famous for its enormous vermilion torii gate and spacious gardens inspired by the Heian period.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - taken off Day 18 on 17 Oct 2026 (Yasaka covers the shrine visit on Day 18; Fushimi Inari on Day 21)
Reservation Info: Shrine grounds are free; gardens require admission.

Name: Ishibei-koji Lane
Description: One of Kyoto's quietest preserved lanes, featuring stone paving, wooden buildings, and a peaceful atmosphere.

Name: Kimono Forest (Randen Arashiyama Station)
Description: Over 600 illuminated pillars wrapped in Nishijin-ori kimono fabric patterns, right at the station platform — free, quick, and a nice bookend to the bamboo grove.

Name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
Description: Zen temple famous for its gold-covered pavilion reflected in a pond, one of Japan's most recognizable sights.
Best Time To Visit: ~2:20-3:00pm, by bus or a ~20 min walk from Ryoan-ji. Closes 5:00pm

Name: Luggage pickup - Yamato Transport (艮町860)
Neighborhood: Shinmachi-dori south of Rokujo, Shimogyo Ward - 10-15 min walk from your stay
Hours: 8:00-20:00 daily including Sundays (Yamato office finder, checked 17 Oct 2026)
Description: Collect the forwarded luggage at the 8:00 opening, take it to your stay by Shosei-en (10-15 min walk), then taxi to Kiyomizu-dera. CHECK FIRST: Yamato lists two former counters at this address (新町花屋町営業所 and 河原町七条営業所), and its office finder now redirects both to 下京営業所 (五条烏丸), 東洞院通松原下る大江町 - check the office name on your pickup notice or call 0570-200-000. If it is the Gojo-Karasuma office, it is ~1.5 km north of your stay (20 min walk, 5 min taxi) - take a 5 min taxi each way and Kiyomizu-dera moves to ~9:00.
Best Time To Visit: 8:00am opening - leave your stay ~7:50, bags back at your stay by ~8:30
Reservation Info: Bring the tracking number and ID
Source: User-provided address; hours from Yamato office finder

Name: Kiyomizu-dera Temple
Description: One of Kyoto's most famous temples, known for its wooden stage overlooking the city and beautiful seasonal scenery.
Best Time To Visit: ~8:50am: taxi from your stay ~8:30 (~¥1,200-1,500, 10-15 min) to the top of Gojo-zaka. Main stage and Okunoin terrace first, Otowa waterfall last (its queue builds fastest). Tour buses and school groups arrive ~9:30-10:00

Name: Kobo-san Antique Market (Tōji Temple)
Hours: Monthly on the 21st only, early morning to ~16:00 - Day 21 is Wed 21 Oct, so it is on
Description: Over 1,000 stalls in the grounds of To-ji, 15 min walk from Kyoto Station; held rain or shine. Vintage kimono, ceramics, woodblock prints. Vendors are almost entirely cash only — hit an ATM or convenience store before you go.
Best Time To Visit: ~8:30-9:45am, after Fushimi Inari and breakfast. Then Kintetsu to Kintetsu Nara (from To-ji Station, or walk back to Kintetsu Kyoto), about 50 min - check the route on the day

Name: Kodai-ji
Description: Zen temple known for beautiful landscaped gardens, bamboo grove, and spectacular autumn night illuminations.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - taken off Day 18 on 17 Oct 2026 (its Zen garden and bamboo overlap Ginkaku-ji and Day 19 Arashiyama)

Name: Kyoto Station restrooms
Description: Multiple free restroom clusters across the station's several floors and the adjoining Kyoto Tower building — the most reliable option in the area.

Name: Matcha Roastery
Description: Small matcha café in a residential Uji neighborhood offering a 'roast flight' of light, medium, and dark roasted matcha | Souvenir snack: Tins of Uji matcha powder — the single best food souvenir from this stop.
Best Time To Visit: Weekday afternoon
Must See Highlight: Order the roast matcha flight (light/medium/dark) alongside the matcha Basque cheesecake

Name: Mitsuo (三嶋 陶物師)
Description: One-man pottery studio and shop; Mr. Mishima makes and sells everything himself, serves tea to visitors
Best Time To Visit: ~9:40am, just after its 9:30 opening (Sunday hours not confirmed) - an 8 min detour down Gojo-zaka
Must See Highlight: Ask to see the hashioki (chopstick rests) and small tea cups — all handmade by Mr. Mishima himself; accept the offered cup of hojicha

Name: Monkey Park Iwatayama
Hours: 9:00-16:00 (summit to 16:30); irregular closures and closed in bad weather (Rurubu, checked 16 Oct 2026)
Description: Mountaintop park home to wild Japanese macaques and panoramic views over Kyoto after a 20-30 minute hike.
Best Time To Visit: 9:00 opening to ~10:35, a 20-30 min climb each way. If it is closed for weather, see Tenryu-ji in the morning instead

Name: Nakashimaya
Description: Small family-run restaurant, obanzai home-style Kyoto cooking, counter seating watching the family cook | Souvenir snack: Ask if they sell any bottled dashi or house pickles to go.
Best Time To Visit: Weeknight (reservation required)
Must See Highlight: Order the pork steak and the obanzai (assorted small home-style dishes); sit at the counter to watch the family cook

Name: Nanzen-ji
Description: One of Kyoto's most important Zen temples, known for its massive Sanmon Gate, peaceful gardens, and the historic Meiji-era brick aqueduct.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:40pm, about 10-15 min walk from Ichizawa (or a short taxi). Buildings close ~5pm.
Reservation Info: Grounds are free; some buildings and gardens require admission.

Name: Nishijin Sei Aun
Description: Small owner-run traditional Japanese restaurant in a quiet residential textile district. ORDER: their seasonal kaiseki-style course — reviews specifically praise the whole-crab course when in season, and the fried chicken/potato salad otherwise. | Souvenir snack: None typical — dinner restaurant.
Best Time To Visit: Weeknight (reservation recommended)
Must See Highlight: Book the private room with the sunken kotatsu table and order the seasonal course; ask about their off-menu celebration dishes

Name: Nishijin Textile District
Description: Historic neighborhood famous for Nishijin-ori weaving, producing some of Japan's finest kimono textiles for over 1,000 years.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: 10:00-16:00

Name: Nishiki Tenmangu Shrine restroom (inside Nishiki Market)
Description: Nishiki Market itself has very few public restrooms — this small shrine tucked into the market has one of the only ones directly on the street.

Name: Nishin Soba (Matsuba / Honke Owariya area)
Description: Kyoto-original dish: soba topped with a whole simmered dried herring fillet, invented in Kyoto (a landlocked city) as a way to get protein from preserved fish before refrigeration. Distinct from any soba you'll find elsewhere in Japan. | Souvenir snack: None typical — sit-down dish.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - taken off Day 18 on 17 Oct 2026

Name: Okochi Sanso Villa
Description: Former estate of a Japanese film actor. Less crowded than Tenryū-ji, with a city viewpoint and teahouse.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - taken off Day 19 on 16 Oct 2026 to make room for Nijo Castle

Name: Omen Ginkaku-ji
Hours: Sat/Sun/hol 10:30-16:00 (L.O. 15:30) and 17:00-20:30; weekdays 10:30-18:00; closed Thursdays (Tabelog, checked 18 Oct 2026)
Description: A famous Kyoto noodle restaurant specializing in handmade udon served with seasonal vegetables and dipping sauce. ORDER: the beef udon with tempura, or the omen set (hot dipping noodles with tempura and a tray of seasonings to customize your broth). | Souvenir snack: Bottled dipping sauce if sold retail. Tabelog 3.57.
Best Time To Visit: ~2:35pm lunch, before Ginkaku-ji - Sunday lunch last order is 3:30pm, then closed until 5:00

Name: Philosopher's Path
Description: A peaceful canal-side walking path connecting Ginkaku-ji and Nanzen-ji, famous for cherry blossoms, cafes, and small temples.
Best Time To Visit: ~2:05pm, walking north from Nanzen-ji toward Ginkaku-ji (about 30 min)

Name: Pontocho Alley
Description: Narrow atmospheric alley famous for restaurants, bars, and traditional dining along the Kamogawa River.
Best Time To Visit: May-September (river terrace season) | Best time of day: dinner / late night
Reservation Info: Walking is free; reservations recommended for many restaurants, especially during summer terrace season. Reserve directly with individual restaurants by phone or their websites, especially for summer terrace (kawayuka) seating.

Name: Randen Arashiyama Station restrooms
Description: Free restrooms right at the station, the natural staging point before or after the bamboo grove.

Name: Ryoan-ji Temple
Description: Home to Japan's most famous rock garden, designed around Zen concepts of simplicity and contemplation.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:20-2:00pm: Randen from Arashiyama to Ryoanji station (change at Katabiranotsuji), about 25-30 min. If you are running late, skip it and go straight to Kinkaku-ji

Name: Saga-Toriimoto Preserved Street
Description: Less crowded than central Arashiyama — traditional houses, small shops.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - was the either/or alternative to Monkey Park on Day 19

Name: Sannen-zaka & Ninen-zaka
Description: Beautiful stone-paved streets connecting Kiyomizu-dera with Higashiyama, lined with traditional shops, cafes, and souvenir stores.
Best Time To Visit: ~10:00am - busy by now on a Sunday

Name: Saryo Tsujiri Gion Main Shop
Hours: 10:30-20:30 (L.O. 19:30), no regular closed day (Tabelog, checked 17 Oct 2026)
Description: Historic matcha dessert shop famous for high-quality Uji matcha parfaits and sweets. | Souvenir snack: Matcha/hojicha tins and matcha sweets — well-packaged for travel.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:00pm - opens 10:30, no reservations, so expect a Sunday queue

Name: Shinpuhkan
Description: Stylish shopping complex that blends historic architecture with modern boutiques, cafes, and restaurants.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Shogoin Yatsuhashi Honkan
Description: Kyoto's famous yatsuhashi sweet — cinnamon raw yatsuhashi or seasonal chestnut flavor.

Name: Shoraian
Description: Elegant tofu kaiseki restaurant overlooking the river from a secluded hillside location. ORDER: the full tofu kaiseki course (multi-course, showcasing tofu prepared many different ways) — this is the entire point of coming here, not an à la carte stop.
Best Time To Visit: March - May / October - November
Reservation Info: Reservations strongly recommended. Reserve by phone directly with the restaurant.

Name: Steak Otsuka
Description: Highly regarded wagyu steak restaurant known for premium beef at reasonable prices. ORDER: the Murasawa Sirloin if available (a rare, limited-supply cut) — otherwise their standard A5 wagyu steak set, served sizzling on a hot iron plate with rice and daikon salad. | Souvenir snack: None typical — sit-down restaurant.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round
Reservation Info: Walk-ins only; arrive before opening to secure a spot.

Name: Tenryu-ji Temple
Description: UNESCO World Heritage Zen temple with one of Kyoto's most beautiful gardens overlooking the mountains.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:00-12:40pm, straight after the Shigetsu lunch - Shigetsu is inside the grounds

Name: Miffy Sakura Kitchen Arashiyama (みっふぃー桜きっちん 嵐山店)
Neighborhood: Arashiyama main street, outside Tenryu-ji (Saga-Tenryuji Tsukurimichicho 20-27)
Hours: 10:00-18:00 daily (Wanderlog, checked 18 Oct 2026 - confirm on miffykitchenbakery.jp)
Description: Miffy bakery and gift shop with Japanese-themed Miffy goods you will not find in the regular Miffy shops, plus Miffy-shaped buns to take away.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:40pm, between Tenryu-ji and Randen Arashiyama Station - 10-15 min
Tags: Miffy; character goods; bakery; on the way

Name: The Munch
Description: Legendary rare-coffee kissaten near Takayasu Station - famously strong nel-drip coffee, including a 30-year barrel-aged variety, cozy retro atmosphere, run by owner Mr. Tanaka. Note: this is in Yao City, roughly 45 min from central Osaka (Namba/Dotonbori) - a real detour, not a quick add to your existing Osaka day.

Name: Togetsukyo Bridge
Description: Historic bridge crossing the Katsura River and the symbolic centerpiece of Arashiyama.
Best Time To Visit: ~10:40am, crossing on the walk from Monkey Park to Shigetsu (10-15 min)

Name: Toraya Kyoto Ichijo Store
Description: Kyoto branch of Japan's legendary wagashi maker, serving refined seasonal Japanese sweets with matcha. | Souvenir snack: Yokan (sweet bean jelly) — Toraya's signature product since the 1600s, keeps well and is a genuinely prestigious gift.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Uji
Description: Historic tea town famous for Uji matcha, Byodo-in Temple, and riverside scenery.
Best Time To Visit: April-May / October-November | Best time of day: morning-afternoon

Name: Uji-biyori
Description: Tiny riverside café run by an elderly couple; the owner plays harmonica for guests | Souvenir snack: Matcha sweets and tea, boxed for travel.
Best Time To Visit: Weekend morning (river-view seats)
Must See Highlight: Sit at a seat facing the Uji River with matcha and dessert; ask the owner to play a tune on his harmonica

Name: Walden Woods Kyoto
Description: Minimalist all-white cafe known for excellent coffee and photogenic interiors. ORDER: the canelé with a hand-drip coffee — their most distinctive pairing.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Yasaka Shrine
Description: Kyoto's best-known Shinto shrine, marking the entrance to Gion and serving as the center of the famous Gion Matsuri festival.

Name: Yebiya
Description: Cash-only neighborhood soba/udon shokudo, local favourite, big portions, no English menu. ORDER: the tenzaru soba (cold soba with tempura) or the kitsune udon set — point at the photo menu if needed.
Best Time To Visit: Weekday lunch (arrive early, gets full)
Must See Highlight: Try the kakiage don (large tempura fritter rice bowl) or the tenzaru soba; bring cash and use Google Translate's camera on the menu

Name: 宇治茶漬け とと兎 Tototo
Description: Small ochazuke (tea over rice) restaurant in Uji where you shave your own bonito flakes tableside | Souvenir snack: Ochazuke rice-seasoning packets if sold retail.
Best Time To Visit: Weekday lunch
Must See Highlight: Order the salmon ochazuke and shave your own bonito flakes at the table; try the matcha whisky

Name: Akaha Chai
Hours: Mon 8am-6pm; Tue Closed; Wed-Thu 8am-6pm; Fri-Sat 9am-8pm; Sun 9am-6pm
Description: One-person specialty chai shop near Nara Park, homemade seasonal chai blends, very friendly owner
Best Time To Visit: Weekday afternoon
Must See Highlight: Try the spiced chai (hot or iced) and ask about the current seasonal special, like the pumpkin chai

Name: Coffee Loom
Description: Tiny alley café and roastery run solo by the owner, thoughtful espresso and filter coffee. ORDER: a hand-drip filter coffee of their current single-origin roast. | Souvenir snack: Bagged coffee beans.
Best Time To Visit: Whenever convenient during your Uji stop
Must See Highlight: Order the Italian-style espresso or a filter coffee; if it's quiet, you may catch the owner roasting the next batch on his roasting machine

Name: Edogawa Naramachi
Description: Traditional restaurant specializing in eel dishes in a historic Nara setting. ORDER: the unaju (grilled eel over rice in a lacquered box) — their signature preparation. | Souvenir snack: None typical — sit-down restaurant.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: lunch / dinner
Reservation Info: Reservations recommended. Reserve by phone directly with the restaurant.

Name: Hoo Nyan Boo
Description: Small gift shop themed around cats, owls, and pigs — towels, earrings, coin purses, glass figurines; owner keeps a live owl in-shop
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Check out the live owl in the shop and browse the cat/owl/pig themed handmade goods

Name: Kakinoha Sushi Tanaka, Nara Honten (柿の葉すし本舗たなか なら本店)
Description: Famous Nara specialty sushi wrapped in persimmon leaves, traditionally preserved for travel. Tabelog 3.25 - below your 3.5 bar; it is here only as a cheap walk-in backup. | Souvenir snack: Boxed kakinoha-zushi itself — travels well since it is leaf-wrapped, the definitive Nara food souvenir.
Best Time To Visit: Lunch backup if Seizen has a queue: buy a box to take away and eat in Nara Park

Name: Kasuga Taisha (bonus)
Description: Thousands of bronze and stone lanterns line the approach — a good pairing with Tōdai-ji if you have extra time in Nara.

Name: Kasuga Taisha Shrine
Hours: Grounds open early to evening; main sanctuary special worship 9:00-16:30, ¥500, no regular closed day (Rurubu, checked 18 Oct 2026)
Description: Nara's most important Shinto shrine, famous for thousands of stone and bronze lanterns surrounded by ancient forest.
Best Time To Visit: ~2:05-2:55pm, 15-20 min walk from Todai-ji. Main sanctuary closes 4:30pm
Reservation Info: Shrine grounds free; inner areas require admission.

Name: Kinko-en
Description: 6th-generation family workshop making traditional Nara sumi (ink sticks) by hand using soot, gelatin, and spices, over 1,000 years of tradition
Best Time To Visit: Weekday afternoon
Must See Highlight: Watch the ink-stick-making demonstration by 6th-generation artisan Bokuen Nagano, then make your own ink stick and carve your name into a keepsake box

Name: Kofuku-ji Temple
Description: Historic temple founded by the powerful Fujiwara clan, with national treasures in its halls and museum. The five-story pagoda is under a full-cover scaffold for its restoration (the spire goes back on in 2031), so you will not see it - treat the grounds as a pass-through.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:05pm, walk through the grounds on the way to Nara Park
Reservation Info: Grounds free; museum and halls require tickets.

Name: Kuruminoki
Description: Lifestyle cafe and shop known for homemade food, crafts, and a relaxed countryside atmosphere. | Souvenir snack: Walnut-based sweets, their specialty.
Best Time To Visit: Spring / Autumn | Best time of day: lunch / afternoon

Name: Midoriya
Description: Ceramics shop in Naramachi with handmade pottery from local and regional artists, wide price range
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Look for the sake glasses with traditional hand-painted Nara deer motifs, and the traditional Nara lanterns

Name: Mizutani-chaya
Description: Historic teahouse-style restaurant near Kasuga Taisha and forest paths. ORDER: a bowl of their handmade soba or udon with a side of mochi — the classic teahouse-rest-stop combination here. | Souvenir snack: None typical — teahouse.
Best Time To Visit: Spring / Autumn | Best time of day: lunch

Name: Mount Wakakusa
Description: Small grassy mountain offering one of the best panoramic views of Nara.
Best Time To Visit: Only if time remains - with the market added it usually will not
Reservation Info: Small entrance fee during open seasons.

Name: Nakatanidou
Description: One of Japan's most famous mochi shops, known for dramatic high-speed mochi pounding demonstrations. | Souvenir snack: Fresh mochi if you're eating same-day; otherwise ask about packaged versions.
Best Time To Visit: ~11:50am, a couple of minutes from Seizen along Sanjo-dori, on the way to Kofuku-ji

Name: Nara Nagomikan
Description: Souvenir shop featuring local crafts, sweets, and traditional Nara products.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: afternoon

Name: Nara Park
Description: The iconic park where hundreds of semi-wild deer roam freely among temples, forests, and walking paths.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:25pm, on the walk from Kofuku-ji to Todai-ji

Name: Naramachi
Description: Preserved merchant district with traditional machiya houses, small cafes, craft shops, and local museums.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:20-5:20pm, about 20 min walk down from Kasuga Taisha. Most shops close around 5pm

Name: onwa
Description: Small vegan restaurant in a traditional wooden house upstairs, popular with locals and repeat visitors. ORDER: their vegetable-forward daily set meal — menu changes seasonally, ask staff what's featured that day.
Best Time To Visit: Weekday lunch
Must See Highlight: Order the Vegan Delight Plate and the chocolate banana cake; take your shoes off and sit at the low table upstairs

Name: Poku-Poku
Hours: Lunch 11:15-14:30 (L.O. 13:30), dinner 17:30-20:00; closes when sold out. Closed Tuesdays, Fridays, the 1st Monday and irregular days (Tabelog, checked 18 Oct 2026)
Description: Small, married-couple-run tonkatsu spot in Naramachi using Yamato pork, a locally designated regional brand — only about 12 seats, genuinely local.
Best Time To Visit: ~11:45am lunch, about 10 min walk from Kintetsu Nara Station
Tags: tonkatsu; local; family-run; Tabelog 3.70; Tabelog Tonkatsu 100 2026
Reservation Info: Fully booked for Wed 21 Oct (18 Oct 2026). Reservation only, online via Tabelog

Name: Tonkatsu Seizen (とんかつ清善)
Neighborhood: Near Sanjo-dori, ~5 min walk from Kintetsu Nara (Honkomori-cho 5-1)
Hours: Weekdays 11:00-21:00 (food L.O. 20:30); Sun & holidays 11:00-17:00; no regular closed day (Tabelog, checked 18 Oct 2026)
Description: Tonkatsu restaurant a few minutes from Kintetsu Nara, open all day with no break, so the lunch time can slide. Tabelog 3.42 on its own page (3.52 in the area list). Reviews mention a mixed fry set. Replaced Poku-Poku, which was fully booked (18 Oct 2026).
Best Time To Visit: ~11:00am lunch, straight from Kintetsu Nara (you arrive ~10:45)
Tags: tonkatsu; walk-in; open all day; Tabelog 3.42
Reservation Info: Walk-in. Reservations are accepted online or by phone (0742-95-4108) if you want one

Name: Tōdai-ji (Great Buddha Hall)
Description: World's largest wooden building, housing Japan's largest bronze Buddha. Arrive at opening to beat tour groups.

Name: Todai-ji Temple
Hours: Daibutsuden 7:30-17:30 April-October, last entry 30 min before closing (checked 18 Oct 2026)
Description: One of Japan's most famous temples and a UNESCO World Heritage Site, famous for the Great Buddha statue in the world's largest wooden building.

Name: Torito-te
Description: Small, cozy shop with handmade bag charms, keychains, earrings, and pouches; warm owner
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Pick up a handmade sewed keychain or bag charm — reviewers say they hold up for years

Name: Akechidaira Ropeway
Description: Cable car viewpoint overlooking Lake Chuzenji, Kegon Falls, and Mount Nantai.
Best Time To Visit: October - November | Best time of day: 10:00-15:00

Name: Futarasan Shrine
Description: Peaceful mountain shrine dedicated to Nikko's sacred mountains, less ornate than Toshogu but more atmospheric.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:50pm, after Toshogu
Reservation Info: Main grounds free; some areas require small fees.

Name: Hippari Dako
Description: Small, casual local restaurant famous with travelers for affordable Japanese comfort food and a fun atmosphere. ORDER: the gyoza and the fried chicken — both specifically praised by reviewers, alongside a cold beer. | Souvenir snack: None typical — sit-down restaurant.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Komekichi Kozushi
Hours: Around lunch and dinner hours; varies by day
Description: Small sushi restaurant offering traditional sushi in a quiet local setting. ORDER: the chef's nigiri set — reviews specifically praise the oysters and fresh seasonal fish selection. | Souvenir snack: None typical — sit-down restaurant.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round
Reservation Info: Reservations recommended, especially dinner. Reserve by phone directly with the restaurant, especially for dinner.

Name: Lake Chuzenji & Kegon Falls
Hours: Lake open 24 hours; waterfall hours vary
Description: One of Nikko's most scenic areas, featuring a mountain lake formed by volcanic activity and one of Japan's most famous waterfalls. FIRST STOP OF THE DAY: take the bus from Tobu-Nikko Station straight after the 8:25am arrival (8:30 or 8:45 on the 2025 timetable, ~50 min without traffic, 1,250 yen). See Kegon Falls (elevator 8:00-17:00, 600 yen) and the lake shore, and be on a bus down by ~10:50am so you reach Shinkyo before the 12:30pm lunch. Going up early avoids the worst of the Irohazaka traffic on this holiday Saturday. Return train: Spacia X 12 leaves Tobu-Nikko 5:44pm (Asakusa 7:35pm).
Best Time To Visit: ~9:30-10:50am, before lunch
Reservation Info: Free; elevator to Kegon Falls observation area requires ticket.

Name: Nikko Castella Honpo
Description: Long-established confectionery shop selling castella sponge cake and traditional Japanese sweets. | Souvenir snack: Castella sponge cake, boxed — a classic regional gift sweet.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Nikko Coffee
Description: Local specialty cafe group known for renovated historic buildings, coffee, and relaxed atmosphere. ORDER: the omurice or curry from their lunch set, paired with a house-roasted coffee and their cheesecake for dessert. | Souvenir snack: Bagged coffee beans.
Best Time To Visit: April - November

Name: Nikko Kariman
Description: Popular local sweet shop known for fried manju (sweet bean-filled cakes). | Souvenir snack: Yuba manju (sweet filled buns) — the definitive Nikko sweet souvenir.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:25pm after Futarasan (closes 5pm), then bus or a 30 min walk to the station for the 5:44pm train

Name: Nikko Tamozawa Imperial Villa Memorial Park
Description: Former imperial summer residence combining Edo, Meiji, and Taisho architecture with beautiful gardens.
Best Time To Visit: April - May / October - November | Best time of day: 9:00-12:00

Name: Nikkō Tōshō-gū
Description: Elaborately carved shrine complex, UNESCO site. Mountain-Japan alternative to the coast.

Name: Nikko Toshogu Shrine
Description: Japan's most lavishly decorated shrine and UNESCO World Heritage Site, dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu, founder of the Tokugawa shogunate. Famous for intricate carvings, gold leaf details, and the Three Wise Monkeys.
Best Time To Visit: ~2:20-3:45pm (last entry 4:30pm)

Name: Nikko Yuba Zen
Description: Restaurant specializing in Nikko's famous yuba cuisine (tofu skin), a local specialty connected to Buddhist temple cuisine. | Souvenir snack: Dried yuba sheets — Nikko's namesake product, packs flat and keeps well.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Rinnoji Temple
Description: Important Buddhist temple complex near Toshogu with a famous golden-lacquered Sanbutsudo hall.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:45pm, straight after lunch

Name: Shinkyo Bridge
Description: Iconic red lacquer bridge marking the entrance to Nikko's sacred area, one of Japan's most photographed bridges.
Best Time To Visit: ~11:40am, getting off the bus from Chuzenji; 3 min walk to the 12:30pm lunch
Reservation Info: Viewing is free; crossing requires a small fee.

Name: Yuzawaya Coffee Shop
Description: Small traditional coffee shop near the historic district, ideal for a quiet break after sightseeing.
Best Time To Visit: October - November

Name: About A Pond
Description: High-quality secondhand boutique in Horie, Osaka's fashion district — curates carefully selected pieces bought from individuals with strong personal style, rather than bulk-buying. Focuses on Japanese labels like Drawer (United Arrows' high-grade select line) and BLAMINK — small, design-focused brands over big logos.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:55pm in Kitahorie, 10 min west of LiLo - closes 7pm
Tags: secondhand; small designers; Japanese brands; curated

Name: Aizuya Honten
Description: The original creator of takoyaki, serving the classic version without sauce to highlight the savory batter. | Souvenir snack: None typical — sit-down restaurant.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Akari Soba
Description: A quiet, homey soba shop tucked away from Dotonbori's crowds — good tempura and soba if you want a calm break from the street-food circuit.
Best Time To Visit: Lunch

Name: Amerikamura (America Village)
Description: Osaka's center for youth culture, vintage clothing, sneakers, streetwear, music, and independent fashion.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:30pm, walk through on the way from Horie to Shinsaibashi-suji

Name: Den Den Town
Description: Osaka's electronics and pop-culture district, often compared to Tokyo's Akihabara.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: afternoon

Name: Dotonbori
Description: Osaka's most famous entertainment district, known for neon signs, street food, restaurants, canals, and the iconic Glico Running Man sign. Dinner is unbooked: wander and walk in here or in Hozenji Yokocho next door.
Best Time To Visit: ~6:45pm - find dinner on the walk (no booking), then the canal and neon

Name: Dotonbori / Shinsekai / Kuromon Market
Description: Osaka's food-focused alternative day: neon canal-side dining district plus a working food market. 30 min from Kyoto.

Name: HAIKU COFFEE ROASTERS
Description: Small specialty coffee roastery run by a couple, Hawaii-inspired décor, low-key neighborhood vibe
Best Time To Visit: Weekday afternoon
Must See Highlight: Try a single-origin pour-over (ask what's fresh that day) and the banana cake; ask to see the roasting machine in action

Name: Hedy Vintage Shop Osaka
Description: Curated vintage luxury and designer resale shop with a well-organized, non-overwhelming selection
Best Time To Visit: Optional, a few minutes from About A Pond in Horie (daily 11am-8pm). Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Look for curated luxury pieces like Celine, Gucci, or Jil Sander at prices well below original retail

Name: Hozen-ji Temple
Description: Small temple best known for its moss-covered Fudo Myoo statue, where visitors splash water for good fortune.
Best Time To Visit: Evening, at the end of Hozenji Yokocho

Name: Hozenji Yokocho
Description: A narrow stone alley lined with traditional restaurants and lanterns, offering a glimpse of old Osaka just steps from bustling Dotonbori.
Best Time To Visit: Evening - a good lane to pick a walk-in dinner, 2 min from Dotonbori

Name: i・yu art space coffee roastery
Description: Tiny roastery/gallery run solo by a woman roaster; art, postcards, and coffee in a cozy space
Best Time To Visit: Weekday morning
Must See Highlight: Get the Yemen drip coffee and place a sticker on the map marking where you're from; browse the 2D art and postcards

Name: Kuromon Ichiba Market
Description: Osaka's most famous food market, known as "Osaka's Kitchen," featuring seafood, wagyu, fruit, and street food. Note: has become touristy in recent years with some vendors pricing for tourists — the seafood and produce stalls are still genuinely good, just be selective. | Souvenir snack: Dried seafood snacks or a vacuum-packed grade of wagyu jerky from a reputable stall.
Best Time To Visit: ~9:15-10:15am, first stop - graze here for breakfast (9-11am is the best window). Leave Kyoto by ~8:00 (roughly 1h15 to Nippombashi)

Name: LiLo Coffee Roasters
Hours: 11:00-23:00, no regular closed day (Walkerplus, Oct 2023 - not rechecked)
Description: One of Osaka's best specialty coffee shops, popular with locals and travelers.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:30pm, first stop after the subway south to Shinsaibashi (about 25 min from Nakazakicho)

Name: Mel Coffee Roasters
Description: Small specialty coffee shop known for carefully prepared pour-over coffee.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: morning

Name: Namba Yasaka Shrine
Description: Small shrine famous for its enormous lion-head stage, believed to swallow evil spirits and bring success.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Osaka Castle
Description: One of Japan's most famous castles, associated with Toyotomi Hideyoshi and the unification of Japan.
Best Time To Visit: ~11:15am-12:45pm, walking north from Karahori via Tanimachi
Reservation Info: Park free; castle museum requires admission.

Name: Pauhana Coffee
Description: Tiny one-man coffee shop and roastery, owner trained in Maui-style coffee, 8 seats inside
Best Time To Visit: Weekday morning
Must See Highlight: Order a flat white or single-origin drip coffee and the warm donut — reportedly one of the best donuts in Osaka

Name: Pigsty Osaka
Description: One of Japan's best-known vintage stores, offering curated American vintage clothing, denim, and military pieces.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: POPEYE vintage used clothing
Description: Small woman-owned vintage clothing shop specializing in women's wear and mid-century American goods
Best Time To Visit: Optional, a few minutes from Osaka Naniwaya in Nakazakicho (daily 1-8pm). Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Browse the mid-century American 50s goods display alongside the remade vintage clothing pieces

Name: Shinsaibashi Shopping Street
Description: Osaka's most famous shopping street with fashion, cosmetics, department stores, and local shops.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:30-5:10pm, or after dinner (most shops open to 9pm)

Name: Shinsekai
Description: Retro Osaka neighborhood famous for Tsutenkaku Tower, kushikatsu restaurants, old-school arcades, and nostalgic atmosphere.
Best Time To Visit: Optional after dinner - about 15 min south of Dotonbori. Skip it if tired: Day 21 starts at To-ji around 7am

Name: Takoyaki Wanaka Dotonbori (たこ焼き道楽 わなか 道頓堀店)
Description: Dotonbori branch of one of Osaka's best-known takoyaki shops, serving crispy-outside, creamy-inside octopus balls. Takeaway counter plus seats upstairs. Tabelog 3.49 (865 reviews, checked 13 Oct 2026). | Souvenir snack: Their takoyaki sauce, bottled.
Best Time To Visit: Evening snack - closes 9pm. Last train to Kyoto 23:59 (JR local, Kyoto 00:43)

Name: Tenjinbashisuji Shotengai
Description: Japan's longest covered shopping arcade (2.6km), where Osaka locals actually shop — a real counterpoint to Dotonbori's tourist-facing strip. Old-school shokudo (diners), produce stalls, and small izakaya lining the whole stretch, minimal tourist presence. | Souvenir snack: Whatever catches your eye along the 2.6km arcade — genuinely local finds, not curated for tourists.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:10-2:30pm: Tanimachi Line from Tanimachi 4-chome to Minami-morimachi (2 stops), then walk north through the arcade to yakiniku lunch at Nikugoro Yokocho (5-chome)
Tags: local market; authentic; shotengai; not touristy

Name: Tsutenkaku Tower
Description: Osaka's nostalgic landmark overlooking Shinsekai, with observation decks and the famous Billiken statue said to bring good luck.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: sunset / evening

Name: YAMASTORE
Description: Quirky vintage and nostalgia shop with upcycled home decor and unique clothing pieces
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Browse the upcycled home decor and nostalgic novelty items alongside the vintage clothing racks

Name: 古着屋KROOL
Description: Small secondhand clothing shop down a back alley in Nakazakicho, carefully curated pieces at excellent prices
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Check the shop's regular opening sales/discounts; note the steep stairs at the entrance

Name: 小泉商店 (Koizumi Shoten)
Description: Old-fashioned takoyaki stand run solo by an elderly woman, extremely cheap, local neighborhood favorite for generations
Best Time To Visit: Weekday afternoon
Must See Highlight: Order the classic takoyaki (4 for ¥100) — a chewier, old-fashioned style unlike the gooey modern Osaka version

Name: Shirakawago Observatory
Description: Best panoramic viewpoint overlooking the entire village and surrounding mountains.
Best Time To Visit: January - February / October - November | Best time of day: morning / sunset

Name: Shiraogi
Description: Takeout counter for gohei mochi (grilled skewered rice with a sweet miso glaze) and Hida beef croquettes — the two defining snacks of a Shirakawa-go visit. Affordable and quick, good for eating on a bench with a view of the gassho-zukuri farmhouses.
Best Time To Visit: Anytime, good after the viewpoint walk
Tags: gohei mochi; Hida beef; street food; regional specialty

Name: Soba Dojo Restaurant
Description: Handmade soba in the center of Ogimachi village, made from locally grown buckwheat. Simple, self-service, friendly. Arrive early — popular spots in the village sell out or develop long queues by midday since options are limited.
Best Time To Visit: Arrive right at opening or before 11:30
Reservation Info: Walk-in, arrive early to avoid a wait

Name: 今昔 (Konjaku)
Description: Run by an elderly couple in a charming thatched-roof building, the first eatery you'll reach crossing the Deai Bridge into the village. Cozy and welcoming; the wagyu set sells out early and is the highlight, with the noodle dishes as a solid secondary option.
Best Time To Visit: Arrive early — the wagyu set sells out

Name: Ebisu Soba
Hours: Varies; typically closed one weekday, check locally
Description: Local favorite soba shop known for handmade buckwheat noodles served with a savory dipping sauce, a simple family-run spot popular with locals.
Best Time To Visit: Weekday lunch to avoid queues
Must See Highlight: Order the cold zaru soba to taste the handmade noodles at their best
Reservation Info: Walk-in; expect a wait at peak lunch hours

Name: Ekiben on the Wide View Hida (Takayama to Nagoya)
Description: Hida-beef ekiben sold at Takayama Station, meant for the scenic limited express ride toward Nagoya — mountain and river views out the window while you eat, a nice way to spend the long transfer day rather than treating it as dead time.
Best Time To Visit: Before boarding
Reservation Info: Walk-in, buy at the station kiosk before boarding

Name: Hida Kotteushi
Hours: 10:00-17:00 (GLTJP lists no regular closed day; the older Tabelog listing says closed Tuesdays)
Description: Popular spot for trying premium Hida beef in casual street-food form: Hida beef nigiri served on a senbei cracker from a takeout counter. Has moved within Sanmachi, to Kamisannomachi 82. Tabelog 3.68 (704 reviews). | Souvenir snack: None - eat it on the spot.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:25pm in Sanmachi

Name: Jinya Dango
Neighborhood: Old Town (Honmachi 1-chome, across from Takayama Jinya)
Description: Small mom-and-pop stand near Takayama Jinya famous for its skewered mitarashi-style dango dumplings, grilled to order over charcoal and glazed with a savory-sweet soy sauce. Tabelog 3.57 (366 reviews). If you already had dango at the Miyagawa market, one stick here is plenty. | Souvenir snack: Their dango if freshly made that day; otherwise skip, doesn't keep.
Best Time To Visit: ~9:50am, straight after Takayama Jinya - closes 3:00pm
Must See Highlight: Eat the dango warm off the grill while strolling the old town streets

Name: Jinya-mae Morning Market
Description: Smaller morning market located directly in front of Takayama Jinya, convenient for combining with sightseeing. | Souvenir snack: Same as Miyagawa — hoba miso, pickles, local sake.
Best Time To Visit: ~8:20am, a quick look before Takayama Jinya opens at 8:45

Name: Kusakabe Folk Museum
Description: Former merchant residence displaying Edo-period household objects, Buddhist art, and traditional architecture.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Kyouya
Description: Family-run restaurant in Takayama's old town since 1979, run by Hida native Kyoko Nishimura; known for hoba miso — local red miso mixed with wild mountain vegetables and mushrooms, grilled tableside on a dried magnolia leaf, a dish she grew up eating. Also serves it combined with Hida beef. Tabelog 3.33 (112 reviews) - below your 3.5 line. | Souvenir snack: Jarred hoba miso paste to take home and grill yourself.
Best Time To Visit: ~11:15am, walk-in - lunch ends 2:00pm
Tags: hoba miso; regional specialty; family-run; local
Reservation Info: Reservations only accepted for dinner - if using for lunch, walk-in only.

Name: Miyagawa Morning Market
Description: One of Japan's best morning markets, selling local produce, crafts, pickles, sweets, flowers, and snacks along the river. BREAKFAST: try Takayama-style mitarashi dango (grilled rice dumplings with a savory soy glaze, not sweet like the Tokyo version) - Nishiya Kajibashi (二四三屋 鍜治橋店, right at the market entrance near Kajibashi bridge, 8am-5:30pm) is a well-regarded, genuinely local vendor with fresh-grilled dango. | Souvenir snack: Hoba miso paste (jarred) and pickled vegetables from the stalls.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:30am - breakfast from the stalls, then 8 min walk south to the Jinya

Name: Ranka Coffee
Description: Classic kissaten-style cafe with a retro atmosphere and traditional Japanese coffee culture.
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon in Sanmachi, next door to Pudding-tei

Name: Sakurayama Hachimangu Shrine
Description: Takayama's most important shrine and home of the famous Takayama Autumn Festival.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:30pm, about 4 min walk north from Kyouya

Name: Sanmachi Suji Historic District
Description: Takayama's most famous historic neighborhood, featuring preserved Edo-period merchant houses, sake breweries, craft shops and cafes. [This is the historic street itself — a district to walk through, not one address.] Also a genuine shopping stop, not just a walk-through - hand-carved chopsticks, Hida lacquerware, local handcrafts, and free sake tastings at the breweries along the street. Most shops close by 5pm. Snack-wise, look out for gohei mochi (grilled rice cakes on a stick, brushed with sweet-savory sauce), mitarashi dango, and Hida beef sushi/skewers sold at small stalls along the street - no need to seek out one specific vendor, they're everywhere.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:20pm, about 11 min walk south from Sakurayama - most shops close by 5pm

Name: Sukeharu Butcher Shop
Hours: 10:00-17:00; closed Tuesdays (Wanderlog - not on an official page)
Description: Mom-and-pop Hida beef butcher shop selling street-food-style juicy Hida beef minced cutlets and croquettes to eat while walking the old town.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:45pm, at the south end of Sanmachi - closes 5:00pm
Must See Highlight: Grab a freshly fried Hida beef minced cutlet to eat street-food style

Name: Suzuya
Description: Long-standing restaurant in a traditional wooden merchant house, known for Hida beef sukiyaki cooked tableside in a cast iron pot — a warmer, homier alternative to the more famous Maruaki (which has notorious no-reservation lines).
Best Time To Visit: Dinner
Tags: sukiyaki; traditional; Hida beef; less crowded than Maruaki
Reservation Info: Walk-in only for now - the restaurant has suspended advance reservations (checked 5 Oct 2026). Arrive near the 17:00 opening.

Name: Takayama Jinya
Hours: 8:45-17:00 (Mar-Oct); no regular closed day in October
Description: The only remaining Edo-period government office of its kind in Japan, showing how local administration worked during the Tokugawa era.
Best Time To Visit: 8:45am opening, about an hour

Name: Takayama Pudding-tei
Description: Small specialty shop famous on social media for its visually striking, silky Japanese-style puddings, a favorite sweet stop while strolling the old town. Tabelog 3.49 (179 reviews).
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon in Sanmachi - closes 4:00pm
Must See Highlight: Try the classic caramel pudding, served in a jar you can eat on the spot

Name: Takayama Shunkei Kaikan
Description: Small museum and shop dedicated to Hida Shunkei — Takayama's amber-toned lacquerware, which lets the wood grain show through the lacquer rather than hiding it.

Name: Takayama Station restrooms
Description: Clean, free, and the obvious meeting point before heading into Sanmachi Suji.

Name: Yoshijima Heritage House
Description: Beautifully preserved merchant house showcasing exceptional traditional Japanese carpentry.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: 2nd Street Reuse Shop
Description: Casual secondhand chain, many branches citywide — surprisingly deep selection of smaller quality-focused Japanese leather brands (Tsuchiya Kaban, Porter, HERZ) at accessible prices, alongside bigger names. Better hunting ground for craft-brand pieces than the big luxury-focused boutiques.
Best Time To Visit: ~2:45pm at the Harajuku flagship, 4 min from Meiji-jingumae Station

Name: a little place coffee
Description: Tiny cafe in a quiet residential street north of Sensoji, excellent pour-over coffee and scones | Souvenir snack: Drip coffee bags, good flat-pack souvenir.
Best Time To Visit: Weekday morning
Must See Highlight: Get the pour-over coffee and a scone; sit at the small upstairs seating if available

Name: Airport restrooms (post-security)
Description: Both Narita and Haneda have plentiful, very clean free restrooms throughout every terminal, including post-security — no need to plan around this one.

Name: Ameyoko Market
Description: Post-war black-market street, now lively shopping. Seafood stalls, dried fish, snacks, cosmetics, small bars. Stalls are mostly cash only.

Name: Ameyoko Shopping Street
Description: Bustling market street under the train tracks with bargain shopping, seafood, snacks, and local atmosphere. | Souvenir snack: Dried snacks, senbei, or discounted candy from the bulk bins — great grazing souvenirs.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center
Description: Kengo Kuma-designed building directly across from Kaminarimon. Clean free restrooms on multiple floors, plus a free rooftop terrace with a Sensō-ji/Skytree view — best two-for-one stop in Asakusa.

Name: Asakusa Kagetsudo
Description: Famous shop known for oversized melon bread and a classic Asakusa street snack experience. | Souvenir snack: Their melon-pan (Japanese sweet bun) — famous for this exact item, buy fresh.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Asakusa Kibi Dango Azuma
Description: Tiny stall right on Nakamise-dori — five warm skewered mochi dumplings rolled in kinako (soybean flour) for a few hundred yen. Cash only, eat standing at the counter. | Souvenir snack: Best eaten fresh on the spot — doesn't travel.

Name: Bamboo Craft Shop Midoriya
Description: Small bamboo craft shop; owner is a bamboo-weaving craftsman whose baskets have been exhibited at the MET
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Buy a pair of handmade bamboo chopsticks; ask the owner to show you his basket work — some pieces have museum-quality craftsmanship

Name: Chicago Shimokitazawa
Description: Vintage store with a genuinely large used-kimono and yukata section alongside Western vintage — a good place to find an affordable real kimono rather than a tourist rental. Card accepted.

Name: Coffee Wrights Kuramae
Description: Hand-drip coffee and a seasonal pastry in a converted warehouse space. | Souvenir snack: Bagged coffee beans.

Name: Costco Wholesale Kawasaki
Description: Japan's Costco carries the familiar Kirkland lineup alongside Japan-specific bulk snacks and a food court. A short taxi/bus ride from Kawasaki Station, and one of the closest branches to Haneda.
Best Time To Visit: Go at the 10:00 opening - Day 24 is a Saturday, the busiest day of the week here
Price: Varies; note membership required to shop, or go with a member
Must See Highlight: Bring a large suitcase or duffel — bulk sizes don't travel well in carry-on
Reservation Info: Membership required (day passes not usually available)

Name: Daikanyama T-Site
Description: Beautiful lifestyle complex centered around one of Tokyo's best bookstores, with cafes, design shops, and architecture.
Best Time To Visit: ~9:45-10:50am, first stop after Haneda - the bookstore is open from 9:00, before the shops

Name: Daikoku-ya
Description: Old husband-and-wife senbei shop; rice crackers hand-made on the premises | Souvenir snack: Senbei rice crackers, sold in gift boxes.
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Buy the shoyu (soy sauce) senbei fresh off the fire and watch the toasting process in-store

Name: Depachika food halls (Mitsukoshi / Daimaru / Takashimaya)
Description: Japanese department-store basements are food halls — sushi boxes, bento, wagashi, seasonal desserts. Daimaru at Tokyo Station is the one to use on arrival (same building as the Kit Kat shop), and a bento from here works as an easy travel-day dinner. Budget ¥800–3,000 for a good bento or sushi box; card is fine here even though the stalls upstairs at outdoor markets are often cash only. | Souvenir snack: This is THE place for boxed sweets souvenirs — wagashi, senbei, regional specialties from across Japan all under one roof, beautifully gift-wrapped.
Best Time To Visit: On arrival (Fri Oct 23): ~4:30pm with the 10:34am train from Kinosaki, which reaches Tokyo around 3:45pm. With the 12:31pm train you arrive around 5:45pm, so go straight here - Daimaru closes ~8pm

Name: Ekiben at Ueno Station
Description: Ueno Station has a good ekiben selection near the Shinkansen platforms — a relaxed way to eat while your train gets underway.
Best Time To Visit: Before boarding
Must See Highlight: Pick a bento from the region you just left (Tokyo-style) or the region you're headed to (Hokuriku) — both are on offer
Reservation Info: Walk-in, arrive a bit early as popular ones sell out

Name: Flamingo Shimokitazawa
Description: One of Tokyo's best-known vintage clothing chains, with a strong Shimokitazawa flagship — American workwear, band tees, denim. Card accepted.

Name: Ginza department store restroom floor (Mitsukoshi)
Description: Reliable, very clean restroom floor inside Mitsukoshi Ginza — the standard fallback for this area.

Name: Harmonica Yokocho
Hours: Most shops 17:00-late night; some daytime shops
Description: Tiny alley filled with old-school izakaya, standing bars, and small restaurants near Kichijoji Station.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: HERZ Flagship (Shibuya)
Description: Long-running Japanese leather brand known for simple, durable everyday bags and wallets made in-house, with an on-site workshop visible from the shop floor. Genuinely in Shibuya/Jingumae, not Kuramae as earlier labeled.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:15pm (opens 12:00), a short walk from SOU・SOU
Reservation Info: Walk-in. To check stock or hold an item (up to ~1 week), call 03-3406-1471 with the product code

Name: Inokashira Park
Description: Beautiful urban park with a pond, walking paths, boats, temples, and seasonal scenery, one of Tokyo's best neighborhood escapes.
Best Time To Visit: March - April / November - December | Best time of day: 8:00-11:00 / 15:00-17:00

Name: Isetatsu
Description: Chiyogami (patterned washi paper) shop running since 1864 — one of the last of its kind in Tokyo. Small paper goods, boxes, and notebooks from a few hundred yen; a genuinely old-standing family craft shop, not a souvenir chain.

Name: Japanese souvenir store ~YOSHIKIRI~
Description: Small souvenir shop curating handmade, made-in-Japan goods rather than mass-produced items; run by a friendly owner
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Look for the handmade handkerchiefs, coin bags, and small dolls; ask the owner which pieces are locally handmade

Name: Kakimori
Description: Genuine hands-on workshop, not just a shop - you personally select the cover, paper, binding, and closure to build a custom notebook you'll actually use, plus an optional Ink Stand upstairs where you mix your own custom ink color. Exactly the kind of 'make something you'd use' stationery craft experience, in Kuramae.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:30-1:15pm, a 15-20 min walk east from Torizune; leave by 1:20pm for the 2:00pm appointment

Name: Kama-Asa
Description: Kappabashi's best-known knife shop — santoku, petty, and deba knives, with engraving.

Name: Kameju
Hours: ~9:00–18:00, popular items sell out — go early
Description: One of Asakusa's famous wagashi shops. Dorayaki: two fluffy pancakes with red bean paste. Try the black sugar version too. | Souvenir snack: Dorayaki (their specialty sweet pancake) — best fresh, but sold in short-dated packs for same-week travel.

Name: Kawasaki Station area breakfast
Description: Optional backup if the Tsukiji breakfast reservation does not work out, or a quick stop if anyone needs something more before continuing to Yokohama.
Best Time To Visit: Morning

Name: Kayaba Coffee
Description: Historic kissaten cafe in a restored wooden building, a great stop for retro Tokyo atmosphere. | Souvenir snack: Bagged coffee beans.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round

Name: Kikumi Senbei
Description: Small local rice-cracker shop with soy sauce, green tea, and sweet flavors | Souvenir snack: Their namesake hand-baked senbei — buy the mixed box.
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Pick up a mixed bag of soy sauce and green tea senbei to snack on while walking Yanaka Ginza

Name: Kimono Hazuki
Description: Small neighborhood shop specializing in well-preserved antique and vintage kimono, patient unhurried service
Best Time To Visit: Weekday afternoon
Must See Highlight: Ask staff to unfold several kimono styles to compare; formal silk pieces run higher but jacket-style haori start affordably

Name: Koenji
Description: More local than Shimokitazawa — vintage stores, punk culture, neighborhood bars. Yakitori and standing bars at night.

Name: KOMEHYO (pre-owned department store)
Description: One of Japan's largest reuse department stores; multiple floors of pre-owned watches from budget to high-end, plus leather bags and other goods — good one-stop option if small stalls feel overwhelming. Good option for a time-constrained last morning - one multi-floor store covering watches, leather, and secondhand in a single stop, rather than hopping between several small shops.
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon

Name: Koroku Seafood Bowl Kuramae
Description: Seafood rice bowl (kaisendon) specialty shop, 3-minute walk from Kuramae Station. Signature move: after eating two-thirds of the bowl, ask for sea bream dashi broth poured over the rest to make a chazuke finish.

Name: Little Pool Coffee
Description: Hidden-alley cafe near Omotesando Station, famous for extremely fluffy, creamy omurice (choose 'fluffy' or 'creamy' style). Day 26 lunch and coffee stop. Expect a queue - a 2022 local guide says there is one all day.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:10pm, straight from Daikanyama: Tokyu Toyoko Line to Shibuya, Ginza Line one stop to Omotesando, then 5 min walk (~20 min). Closes on irregular days - check Instagram the day before

Name: SOU・SOU KYOTO Aoyama Store
Description: SOU・SOU's Tokyo shop: Japanese-pattern textiles, clothing, jika-tabi and tabi socks in the Kyoto brand's prints. The kids' line (Warabegi) is only listed at the Kyoto shops; a 2022 article mentions kids' sizes of tabi socks here, not confirmed for now.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:45-1:00pm, a few minutes' walk from Little Pool

Name: Maker's Watch Knot Kichijoji Gallery Shop
Description: Knot's original gallery store with a full-open display concept, in the leafy Kichijoji neighborhood; pairs well with a stroll through nearby Inokashira Park.
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon

Name: Maker's Watch Knot Omotesando Gallery Shop
Hours: 11:00-19:00, no regular closed days in October
Description: Global flagship of Knot, a Tokyo-founded brand letting you customize a Made-in-Japan watch head with straps from different regional artisans; approachable price point with ~200 models on display and in-store case-back engraving.

Name: Matsushima Izakaya
Description: Extremely affordable 24-hour izakaya, every item priced at 335-350 yen, generous portions, Showa-era atmosphere. Note: multiple 'Matsushima' establishments exist across Tokyo (Ikebukuro, Shinjuku-sanchome yakitori, Yoyogi-Uehara Chinese) - this is the best-documented match for a classic izakaya experience, but worth confirming which one was originally intended.

Name: Mimasu
Description: Likely refers to Mimasuya, one of Tokyo's oldest izakayas (opened 1905) - fourth-generation-owned, yakitori/tamagoyaki/agedashi tofu plus rarer dishes like stewed whole loaches, faded handwritten menus, tatami seating. Exact neighborhood unconfirmed - worth verifying before relying on this.

Name: Nakamise Shopping Street
Description: Historic shopping street leading to Senso-ji with traditional snacks and souvenirs.
Best Time To Visit: March - May / October - November | Best time of day: 9:00-12:00

Name: Nakano Broadway
Description: Legendary multi-floor shopping complex famous for collectibles, vintage toys, manga, anime goods, used watches, and unique Japanese subculture finds.
Best Time To Visit: Year-round | Best time of day: 12:00-17:00

Name: Ginza Tamai (銀座 玉ゐ)
Neighborhood: Ginza 6-chome, Kojun Building 4F - 3-4 min walk from Ginza Station
Description: Ginza branch of the long-established Nihonbashi anago (saltwater conger eel) specialist - anago is a genuine Tokyo Bay specialty, lighter and less fatty than freshwater unagi. ORDER: the hakomeshi box with both simmered and charcoal-grilled anago, and finish the last third with dashi poured over. Tabelog 3.53 (606 reviews). Chosen over the Nihonbashi main branch because it sits inside the Ginza shopping area.
Best Time To Visit: ~11:15am: Tozai Line from Monzen-nakacho to Nihombashi, then Ginza Line to Ginza (about 20 min). Lunch runs to 3:00pm, so it can also follow the shopping
Tags: anago; conger eel; regional specialty; Ginza; Tabelog verified 3.53
Must See Highlight: Try both the simmered and grilled anago side by side to compare
Reservation Info: Not booked - whether it takes lunch bookings is not confirmed. Phone 03-6264-6896 to ask, otherwise walk in at the 11:00 opening. Backup: the Nihonbashi main branch, 2 stops away on the Ginza Line (lunch is walk-in only there)

Name: Okura
Description: Small indigo-dyed clothing shop in an old Japanese house, made-in-Japan denim and sashiko workwear
Best Time To Visit: 11:00 opening, 5 min walk from T-Site. Weekdays 11:00-19:00
Must See Highlight: Try the traditionally dyed indigo jeans and sashiko pants; ask about alterations done on the spot

Name: Hedy Daikanyama (pre-owned luxury)
Description: Pre-owned designer bags and jewelry, plus some clothing and watches - Celine, Loewe, Bottega Veneta and Prada as well as Chanel. Its online shop lists most pieces around ¥25,000-300,000, so the ~¥75,000 range is well covered. The online listings may not match what is in the Daikanyama shop.
Best Time To Visit: ~11:20-11:45am, two minutes from Okura

Name: Omoide Yokocho
Description: Narrow alley packed with tiny yakitori and izakaya counters dating back to postwar Tokyo.
Best Time To Visit: October - April (cooler weather makes alley dining more enjoyable)
Reservation Info: Most places walk-in; some tiny counters do not take reservations.

Name: RagTag (secondhand fashion, Harajuku)
Description: Well-curated preowned fashion chain — despite the Harajuku name, look past the big-logo pieces here; RagTag carries a genuine mix including quality-over-logo Japanese and European brands (Porter, Il Bisonte, Tsuchiya Kaban, Mulberry) at a more accessible entry point than mega-luxury vintage boutiques.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:45pm on Cat Street
Reservation Info: Walk-in. Optional: send up to 3 items from ragtag.jp to this store to try on (free, 3-5 days, held 7 days, members only) - order by ~Wed 21 Oct

Name: Senso-ji Temple
Description: Opens 6am - moved here from Day 8 since the flight lands 3pm at Narita, making an evening visit unrealistic. Since you're staying in Ueno/Asakusa at the start of the trip, an early visit here before the rest of the day works well.
Best Time To Visit: Early morning, right at 6am open, before crowds

Name: Shimokitazawa
Description: Vintage clothing, records, independent stores in a maze of small alleys. Good curry and coffee too.

Name: Shimokitazawa Station restrooms
Description: Free restrooms at the station, central to both the vintage shopping and Koenji-bound trains.

Name: Sometaro
Description: Old wooden okonomiyaki restaurant — you grill it yourself. Also try yakisoba. | Souvenir snack: None typical — sit-down restaurant.

Name: Sushi Matsue
Description: Widely called Tokyo's best omakase without a Michelin star — a genuine neighborhood counter rather than a prestige Ginza institution, with friendly chefs and a warm, unpretentious welcome. Right in Ebisu, on your existing Day 26 route, so no detour needed.
Best Time To Visit: Evening
Tags: omakase; sushi; neighborhood; craftsmanship; not Ginza
Reservation Info: Reservation required, book once dates are firm

Name: Tokyo Station restrooms (Marunouchi side)
Description: One of the largest, cleanest restroom clusters in the city, spread across several floors — an easy stop after a long transfer.

Name: Traveler's Factory Nakameguro
Description: Flagship of the Traveler's Notebook brand, tucked into a quiet Nakameguro backstreet; a customizable leather notebook cover system with dozens of refill inserts, plus occasional in-store workshops.
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Must See Highlight: Check if a customization workshop is running that day

Name: Ueno Park
Hours: Grounds always open · museums generally ~9:30–17:00, most closed Mon
Description: Best first walk in Japan: museums, shrines, locals exercising, street performers, families. No agenda needed — just adjust.

Name: Ueno Park public restrooms (Shinobazu Pond)
Description: Several free public restrooms scattered through the park; the ones by Shinobazu Pond and near the National Museum are the best kept.
