Name: Ueno Sakuragi Atari
Description: A cluster of three 1938 wooden houses turned into a mini café/bakery/beer/general-store village, a 10-min walk from Ueno Park. Good easy stop on an arrival day when you don't want a plan. | Souvenir snack: Small-batch snacks from the converted-house shops on site.

Name: Ueno Station restrooms
Hours: Station open ~4:30–翌1:00 (restrooms accessible during station hours)
Description: Free, clean, and easy to find near the main concourse and JR ticket gates — the most reliable restroom stop in the neighborhood.

Name: Vintage Kimono Shop
Hours: Hours vary, check ahead (weekends most reliable)
Description: Small vintage kimono shop with reasonably priced used kimonos and antique dolls
Best Time To Visit: Weekend afternoon
Must See Highlight: Browse the vintage kimono racks for bargains; ask about ichimatsu dolls, sold cheaply here

Name: Yanaka Cemetery (bonus)
Description: A quiet, atmospheric walk through Tokyo's most famous old cemetery, if Yanaka Ginza leaves you wanting more.

Name: Yanaka Ginza
Description: One of Tokyo's best-preserved old neighborhoods with traditional stores, temples, cats, and small local businesses.
Best Time To Visit: March - April / October - November | Best time of day: 10:00-16:00

Name: Yanaka Ginza public restroom (Yuyake Dandan)
Description: Free public restroom right at the top of the Yuyake Dandan steps overlooking Yanaka Ginza.

Name: Byōdō-in (optional swap)
Description: Tea-culture day trip alternative, 30 min from Kyoto. Pair with Nakamura Tokichi for a matcha parfait.
Best Time To Visit: ~11:00am. Uji window is ~10:45am-1:15pm, so pick Byodo-in, lunch and one or two tea stops

Name: Kanteibyo (Kuan Ti Miao) Temple
Description: Ornate Chinese temple dedicated to Guan Yu, guarded by stone lions; a striking architectural contrast to the Japanese temples elsewhere on the trip. [OPTIONAL - quick 5-min stop if walking past anyway]
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Price: Free (small fee to enter inner hall)

Name: Montbell Yokohama Shin-Yamashita
Description: Montbell's seaside branch near Motomachi-Chukagai Station — same station area as your existing Yokohama Chinatown stop, so it's an easy add to that day without extra travel. [OPTIONAL - only if you still need outdoor gear after the Kyoto Station branch]
Best Time To Visit: Anytime
Tags: outdoor gear; Japanese brand; convenient location

Name: Yamashita Park
Description: Waterfront promenade park with views of the bay and the retired ocean liner Hikawa Maru docked alongside; a relaxed stroll after Chinatown.
Best Time To Visit: On the waterfront walk between Red Brick Warehouse and Chinatown

Name: Yokohama Chinatown
Description: Japan's largest Chinatown, 250+ restaurants and street stalls in a few dense blocks; steamed buns, xiaolongbao, and roasted chestnuts sold straight from the counter. | Souvenir snack: Roasted chestnuts or a box of mooncakes/egg tarts from one of the bakeries. [CORE - walk through after the dim sum lunch at Saiko Shinkan]
Best Time To Visit: ~2:00pm after the dim sum lunch - a walk-through; keep snacks light, dinner at Manchinro is 6:30pm
Must See Highlight: Graze rather than sit down — the counter snacks are the point

Name: Yokohama Coffee Stand
Description: Tiny, coffee-only stand near Chinatown/Motomachi station, run by a dedicated barista who takes real care over each cup. A quiet counterpoint to Chinatown's bustle right before you head into it.
Best Time To Visit: ~2:30pm in the Motomachi-Chukagai area - closes 6pm

Name: Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse (Aka Renga Soko)
Description: Restored early-1900s customs warehouses turned into a craft-and-design shopping and dining complex on the harbor. Good for local craft souvenirs and a coffee break with harbor views.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:45-5:45pm after the Cup Noodles Museum (5 min walk); then 20-25 min on foot or a short taxi back to Chinatown for the 6:30pm dinner

Name: Manchinro Honten
Description: The oldest restaurant in Yokohama Chinatown, opened 1892 - genuine old-guard Cantonese cuisine (Peking duck, dim sum) in an elegant traditional dining room, right in Chinatown, where you already are on Day 24. The whole-group dinner on the last day everyone is together.
Best Time To Visit: 6:30pm - reservation confirmed

Name: Coffee Shop Yamamoto
Description: Long-established coffee shop since 1969, 500m north of Togetsukyo Bridge, home-roasted beans, Showa-era interior with wood walls and leather sofas. The C Set (ham toast sandwiches, scrambled eggs, salad) is a proper savory breakfast, not a sweet pastry spread.
Best Time To Visit: 7:00am opening. Leave your stay ~6:20: walk to Kyoto Station (~15 min), JR Sagano Line to Saga-Arashiyama (~16 min), then a 4 min walk. Check the train times the night before
Tags: kissaten; historic; savory breakfast; not sweet
Must See Highlight: Order the C Set for a proper non-sweet breakfast

Name: BEAMS Women Harajuku
Description: Dedicated women's BEAMS store - three labels under one roof (Ray BEAMS for trend/everyday pieces, International Gallery BEAMS for curated domestic/international designers, Vermeerist BEAMS for special vintage-adjacent pieces). Accessible mid-tier pricing, on the same Harajuku strip as RagTag.
Tags: women's clothing; Japanese brand; select shop; mid-tier; convenient

Name: Nijo Castle
Hours: 8:45-16:00 (last entry), grounds close 17:00. Honmaru Palace closed on the 3rd Monday and the day after - Mon 19 Oct is one
Description: UNESCO World Heritage former residence of the Tokugawa shoguns - famous for its 'nightingale floors' (uguisubari) that chirp underfoot as a security measure against intruders, plus the ornate Ninomaru Palace and its screen paintings.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:20-4:20pm: taxi from Kinkaku-ji (~15 min) or bus (~25 min). Last entry 4:00pm - the tight point of the day. The Ninomaru Palace and nightingale floors are open
Must See Highlight: Walk the nightingale floors slowly to hear them chirp

Name: Day 27 breakfast (near your hotel)
Description: Keep this quick and simple - a real morning window is only about 4-5 hours before you need to leave for Haneda by roughly 1:00-1:15pm (3hr buffer + ~40min travel time for a 4:50pm flight). Grab breakfast near your hotel, then either: (a) head back to any Day 26 shop you didn't finish (RagTag, BEAMS Women Harajuku, 2nd Street, Hedy), or (b) go to KOMEHYO instead for a single efficient stop covering watches/leather/secondhand in one building.
Best Time To Visit: Morning, keep it quick

Name: Quick lunch before Haneda
Description: Keep this simple and fast - a conbini onigiri, a depachika bento, or a quick counter meal near your last stop. Don't plan a sit-down restaurant here; the goal is to be walking toward the station/Haneda by 1:00-1:15pm.

Name: Matsumoto Kiyoshi (drugstore)
Description: Japan's most common drugstore chain, on nearly every block in Tokyo - the best place for everyday/budget skincare (Hada Labo, Biore, Melano CC, Canmake, Kose) at accessible prices, plus tax-free shopping for tourists. Don't need to seek out a specific branch, just pop into any Matsumoto Kiyoshi you pass.
Best Time To Visit: Anytime

Name: @cosme TOKYO
Description: Curated cosmetics/skincare specialty store ranking products by real user reviews - a step up from a drugstore, good for discovering trending Japanese brands with test samples available. Right in Harajuku, on your existing Day 26 route.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:45pm, by Harajuku Station

Name: Baroque Tokyo (haircut)
Description: English-speaking hair salon - all stylists have experience working overseas, genuinely fluent English, not just 'some words.' Specializes in cuts, color, and Japanese straightening. Right in Omotesando, on your existing Day 26 shopping route - book a morning slot (~1-1.5hrs) before the shops open. Note: Bon Hair in Kyoto (Day 17) is scheduled earlier and works for both departure groups - this Tokyo option is more of a backup if Kyoto timing doesn't work out.
Best Time To Visit: Morning, before shops open
Must See Highlight: Book online in advance, especially for a specific time slot

Name: Tokyo Beauty Labo (facial)
Description: Genuinely mid-range facial specialist - booked via Airbnb Experiences, so the whole booking platform is already built around international guests (English interface, verified reviews from foreign travelers). Certified HydraFacial specialist, real prices around $46-52 (~7,000-8,000 yen) for a 45-minute treatment - a fraction of the premium boutique spas in Omotesando. In Shibuya, on your existing Day 26 route.
Best Time To Visit: Morning or early afternoon
Tags: facial; foreigner-comfortable; moderate price; Airbnb Experience

Name: B-Side Label (Yokohama Red Brick Warehouse)
Description: Made-in-Japan sticker brand - high-quality waterproof, UV-protected stickers that genuinely last 3+ years without peeling, 5,000+ designs spanning Pokemon/One Piece collabs to local Japanese motifs, ~200-300 yen each with a free sticker on purchase. This location is inside the Red Brick Warehouse.
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Tags: stickers; collectible; made in Japan; affordable; convenient
Must See Highlight: Ask staff for design recommendations - they know the collection well

Name: B-Side Label (Kanazawa FORUS)
Description: Same B-Side Label sticker brand, this branch is on the 3rd floor of Kanazawa FORUS, the mall beside Kanazawa Station (same building as Mori Mori Sushi on 6F). Waterproof, UV-protected, made in Japan.
Best Time To Visit: Anytime
Tags: stickers; collectible; made in Japan; affordable; convenient

Name: Kit Kat Chocolatory (Tokyo Station)
Description: Boutique Kit Kat shop overseen by patissier Yasumasa Takagi - premium exclusive flavors (Sublime chocolate line, seasonal varieties) with much nicer gift-box packaging than convenience-store Kit Kats. In the basement of Daimaru, directly connected to Tokyo Station. A genuinely good affordable, giftable, uniquely-Japanese food souvenir for a group.
Best Time To Visit: Same trip as the Daimaru food hall - closes 8pm
Tags: Kit Kat; food souvenir; giftable; affordable; convenient
Must See Highlight: Check what's in stock - flavors rotate seasonally and some sell out

Name: Iwata Coffee Shop
Hours: 9:30-18:00, last order ~16:30; closed Tuesdays and the 2nd Wednesday
Description: Historic kissaten established 1945, near Kamakura Station - pale-yellow European-style exterior, cozy brown leather booths that have kept their character for 80 years. Rumored to have been frequented by John Lennon and Yoko Ono. Famous for hot cakes over 3cm thick (20-30 min to cook, and longer waits on busy weekends) alongside sandwiches. Tabelog 3.71.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:22pm - last order is around 4:30pm. If there is a queue, skip it and go on to Kotori

Name: Noge District (dinner alternative)
Description: Yokohama's Showa-era drinking district, a few stops from Chinatown - small izakaya and bars packed into narrow lanes, a good alternative to Manchinro if you want something more casual/local for dinner.
Best Time To Visit: Evening

Name: Bon - Hair (Kyoto)
Description: Private hair salon in a renovated traditional machiya near Nijo Castle - stylist Bon, 27+ years experience, fluent English. IMPORTANT: this is a premium salon (Men's cut ¥8,800-9,900, Ladies ¥11,000-12,100), not an affordable option - genuinely worth it if you want a personalized, unhurried experience, but budget accordingly.
Best Time To Visit: Book ahead for a specific slot
Tags: haircut; English-speaking; premium; machiya; not affordable

Name: Standard neighborhood salon (biyoin) near AEON Mall Kyoto
Description: The genuine middle tier between QB House and a premium boutique - a normal full-service Japanese hair salon (biyoin), cut + shampoo + style, typically 3,500-5,500 yen. These don't market themselves to tourists specifically, but a basic cut doesn't require much conversation, and most stylists are comfortable using a translation app if needed. AEON Mall Kyoto (same building as QB House and Mont-bell, already on your Day 17 route) typically has a standard salon alongside the express one - walk in and ask, or search '美容室' (biyoshitsu) near wherever you're staying for options closer to your hotel.
Best Time To Visit: Weekday afternoon, less likely to need a wait
Tags: haircut; mid-range; full service; comfortable with foreigners
Must See Highlight: Bring a reference photo to minimize the need for detailed conversation
Reservation Info: Walk-in usually fine, or ask your hotel to help book

Name: Gyoza Hohei
Hours: Evening; closed on Sun 18 Oct (reported by you)
Description: Fabulously garlicky pan-fried gyoza right in the middle of Gion, the geisha district. You might spot a maiko or geiko enjoying a plate here too.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - closed on Day 18 (Sun); replaced by Sukemasa on 18 Oct 2026

Name: Ichizawa Shinzaburo Hanpu (一澤信三郎帆布)
Hours: 10:00-18:00, closed Tuesdays (blog summary, checked 18 Oct 2026 - confirm on the official site)
Description: Kyoto's handmade canvas bag maker - bags sewn in the workshop behind the shop, sold only here and online. About 5 min walk from Higashiyama Station, on Higashioji between Gion and Nanzen-ji.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:10pm, walking north on Higashioji from Gion toward Nanzen-ji
Tags: canvas bags; craft; made in Kyoto; workshop brand

Name: Gyoza-dokoro Sukemasa Takatsuji Honten (ぎょうざ処 亮昌 高辻本店)
Neighborhood: Horinouchi-cho 263, Shimogyo Ward - ~7 min walk from Shijo Station (Karasuma Line)
Hours: 11:30-14:00, 17:00-22:00 (L.O. 22:00); open year-round per Hitosara, irregular closures per Gurunavi - call 075-201-6175 to check
Description: Kyoto-style gyoza with ginger, lighter than Hohei's garlicky ones, with small obanzai sides. Tabelog 3.50. On your way home: afterwards take the Karasuma Line from Shijo to Kyoto Station, or walk south.
Best Time To Visit: After dinner, ~15-20 min walk west from Pontocho
Tags: gyoza; ginger; casual; on the way home

Name: Kanazawa Station quick breakfast (before departure)
Description: Alternative to eating in Toyama - grab something quick at Kanazawa Station itself before the early departure. ORDER: a pastry and coffee from one of the station bakeries, or an onigiri from a station convenience store if you're truly pressed for time.
Best Time To Visit: Early morning, before 8am departure

Name: Kurobe Gorge Railway
Hours: Seasonal, late April-November; check current status given post-earthquake repairs
Description: Open-air scenic train through one of Japan's deepest gorges - 40+ tunnels, 20+ bridges, ~80 minutes each way to Keyakidaira. Late October is peak autumn foliage season here. Sit right side going out, left side coming back for best views. Bring layers - open-air cars have no protection from the cold.
Best Time To Visit: 12:50pm train up, 3:19pm train back (about an hour at Keyakidaira)
Tags: scenic train; autumn foliage; unique experience; must book ahead in peak season
Must See Highlight: Book open-air reserved seats 2-3 weeks ahead for late October - they sell out in peak foliage season. Check current operating status - full line to Keyakidaira reopens Oct 1 2026 after bridge repair.
Reservation Info: BOOKED - Unazuki→Keyakidaira 12:50pm-2:12pm; return Keyakidaira 3:19pm, arrives Unazuki ~4:35pm

Name: Kuroya
Description: Cozy izakaya near Kanazawa Station, popular even among locals - locally sourced traditional seafood dishes paired with their own original junmaishu sake. Nostalgic wood-warmed interior. A more casual, closer-to-the-station alternative to Ajidokoro Takasaki.
Best Time To Visit: Evening

Name: Unazuki Onsen station-area shokudo (flexible)
Description: Being upfront: this is a small mountain town and I have not been able to pin down one specific great restaurant here I can confidently vouch for (two attempts already turned out closed/not to your taste). ORDER: whatever soba/udon set looks appealing at the small shokudo clustered right around the station — walk out and see what looks good, or treat Masuzushi (grabbed at Toyama Station) as your reliable lunch and skip a second sit-down meal here entirely.
Best Time To Visit: Midday

Name: Ainokura Village (Gokayama)
Description: The larger of Gokayama's two UNESCO villages - nearly 20 gassho-zukuri farmhouses along a single road, quieter and less touristy than Shirakawa-go despite similar architecture. A 5-10 minute uphill walk from the parking lot reaches the observation viewpoint for the classic panorama shot. Budget about an hour here including the climb.
Best Time To Visit: Morning, first stop after leaving Kanazawa

Name: Suganuma Village (Gokayama)
Description: Smaller Gokayama village, about 10-12 minutes by car from Ainokura - nine houses, an elevator-accessible viewpoint (reliable even in poor weather, unlike Ainokura's uphill climb). A quicker 20-30 minute stop compared to Ainokura's longer visit.
Best Time To Visit: Late morning, after Ainokura

Name: Une Nana Cool (Wacoal, Shibuya Parco)
Description: Wacoal's youth-oriented specialty shop - more trend-forward and affordable than the Ginza DIA line, aimed at a younger customer. One shop directory marks the Shibuya Parco branch as closed (not confirmed); another listing puts une nana cool on Shibuya Hikarie 4F. Check which branch is open before going.
Best Time To Visit: ~5:15pm, across the street from Hands Shibuya (Parco), if that branch is open
Tags: undergarments; lingerie; affordable; convenient; youthful styles

Name: Yojiya (Kiyomizu Sannenzaka)
Description: Kyoto's own cosmetics brand since 1904 - started as a stage makeup shop for the city's theater actors, now famous for aburatorigami (oil-blotting paper), hand cream, and yuzu lip cream. This location sits inside the Seiryu-en Garden, right along your existing Sannenzaka walk in Higashiyama.
Best Time To Visit: ~10:15am, mid-walk through Sannen-zaka - opening time not confirmed
Tags: local brand; cosmetics; consumables; Kyoto since 1904; convenient
Must See Highlight: The aburatorigami oil-blotting paper is the signature item

Name: Hyakumangoku Bento (Kanazawa Station)
Description: A genuinely unique Kanazawa ekiben - crab and salmon roe over pressed sushi (oshizushi), topped with actual gold leaf, tying into Kanazawa's own craft tradition. Sold at Ekiben Dokoro Kanazawa near the station's west exit, alongside other options like Noto beef croquettes and nodoguro onigiri. Ekiben Dokoro Kanazawa opens as early as 5:40am, making this a realistic grab-and-go breakfast before an early departure.
Best Time To Visit: Grab before boarding
Tags: ekiben; crab; gold leaf; not mackerel; unique to Kanazawa
Must See Highlight: Ask specifically for the Hyakumangoku bento if not displayed

Name: Kanizushi (crab pressed sushi ekiben)
Description: Crab meat pressed sushi (oshizushi) - genuinely popular specifically in the Kanazawa/Hokuriku region, not mackerel-based. Simpler and usually cheaper than the Hyakumangoku gold-leaf bento, same shop.
Best Time To Visit: Grab before boarding
Tags: ekiben; crab; not mackerel; regional specialty

Name: Nodoguro onigiri
Description: Rice ball featuring nodoguro (blackthroat seaperch), one of the most prized fish in the region - priced higher than standard onigiri given how sought-after the fish is. A lighter, more portable option than a full bento.
Best Time To Visit: Grab before boarding

Name: Noto beef bento/croquette
Description: A meat-based alternative to the seafood-heavy Kanazawa ekiben lineup - premium Noto beef, either as a full bento or a simpler croquette. Good option if you want something other than fish/crab entirely.
Best Time To Visit: Grab before boarding
Price: yen (moderate to premium depending on format)
Tags: ekiben; beef; not seafood; not mackerel

Name: Kamo Takigohan Ginshari
Description: Duck rice specialist (kamo takigohan — duck cooked into seasoned rice), with a broader fish/meat/sake menu. Opens 6:30am. ORDER: the signature duck rice — duck is a genuine Kanazawa specialty, the same bird behind jibuni.
Best Time To Visit: Early morning, before your Kurobe Gorge departure
Tags: duck rice; local specialty; early opening; convenient timing

Name: Izuei Honten
Description: One of Tokyo's oldest unagi restaurants - 300 years old, mid-Edo period founding, now run by the 9th-generation proprietress. Staff dressed in traditional kimono, soft shamisen music, overlooking Shinobazu Pond. Serves proper Edomae-style unagi (grilled then steamed for a fluffy texture). Historically frequented by novelist Mori Ogai. Genuinely traditional rather than a budget pick - price reflects the pedigree.
Best Time To Visit: Lunch
Price: yen (premium - a proper traditional unagi experience)
Tags: unagi; eel; historic; 300 years; traditional; premium
Reservation Info: Walk-in, expect a 20-30 min wait at lunch

Name: Tenmusu (grab-and-go alternative)
Neighborhood: Near the Shinkansen gates, Nagoya Station
Description: Nagoya's other signature - small rice balls filled with shrimp tempura, sold as boxed sets at multiple shops near the Shinkansen gates (Umaimon-dori/Esca area). A faster alternative to a sit-down hitsumabushi meal if your connection is tight.
Best Time To Visit: If short on time before the Shinkansen to Kyoto
Tags: tenmusu; portable; quick; unique to Nagoya

Name: Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology
Description: Housed in the original 1925 red-brick weaving mill where Sakichi Toyoda began, tracing Toyota's evolution from textile-machinery maker to automotive giant - genuinely substantial exhibits on both textile and automotive technology, plus interactive tech displays. A violin-playing robot performs in the lobby five times daily. 3 min walk from Sako Station (2 min/¥180 from Nagoya Station via Meitetsu Nagoya Line), or ~15-20 min walk. Budget 1.5-2 hours.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:40-3:00pm, after lunch at Kikukawa: Meitetsu from Meitetsu Nagoya to Sako (2 min), or a 15-20 min walk. Last entry 4:30pm. Bags stay in a Nagoya Station locker
Tags: museum; Toyota; industrial history; near Nagoya Station
Must See Highlight: Time your visit for the violin-playing robot performance if it lines up

Name: Unagi Washoku Shirakawa (Joshin)
Neighborhood: Nishi Ward, 2 min from Joshin Station (Tsurumai subway line)
Description: Historic hitsumabushi specialist, serving the dish unchanged for 70+ years. Located 2 minutes from Joshin Station (Tsurumai subway line). ORDER: the hitsumabushi — eaten in three stages (plain, with condiments, then as ochazuke with broth poured over). Closed Thursdays. Walk-in wait is typically 20-30 minutes if no reservation slots remain.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - lunch service ends 14:30
Reservation Info: Try Tabelog online reservation; if unavailable, walk-in historically accepted with a wait
Source: Web Research (Tabelog, Visit Nagoya official site)

Name: Ibasho (いば昇)
Description: Genuine historic alternative to Shirakawa - founded 1909, single location with no branches (unlike chains). Wikipedia itself credits Ibasho, alongside Atsuta Houraiken, as one of the two restaurants where hitsumabushi actually originated, dating the dish to the Taisho era (1912-1926). Tranquil atmosphere with a koi pond and tatami seating. Reservations only required for groups of 5+; smaller parties are expected to simply walk in, making this genuinely more reliable than Shirakawa's limited online booking. From the Toyota museum: Meitetsu from Sako to Nagoya Station (2 min), then the Higashiyama subway to Sakae - about 25 min door to door. Sakae back to Nagoya Station is ~5 min by subway.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - about 25 min from Nagoya Station by subway, so it was replaced by Kikukawa on Day 17 (16 Oct 2026)
Tags: hitsumabushi; historic since 1909; origin restaurant; single location; walk-in friendly for small groups
Must See Highlight: When dining as 2+, hitsumabushi traditionally comes in one large shared ohitsu dish
Reservation Info: Walk-in expected for parties under 5; phone ahead only needed for larger groups
Source: Web Research (Wikipedia, Ibasho official site, multiple independent sources)

Name: Junsei (順正)
Description: Tofu and yuba kaiseki-style cuisine at the Nanzen-ji location, in a beautiful garden setting. ORDER: the grilled yuba and tempura — specifically praised in reviews. One-hour dining limit; reservations recommended.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - taken off Day 18 on 17 Oct 2026
Tags: tofu kaiseki; yuba; verified via Google Places; garden setting; Nanzenji
Must See Highlight: Try the grilled yuba with miso

Name: Kashintei Minokou
Neighborhood: Pontocho, just south of Sanjo (Nakagyo Ward)
Description: Family-run kaiseki restaurant on Pontocho, just south of Sanjo — mother front of house, son as chef. ORDER: the kaiseki course menu. Genuinely good value for the quality.
Best Time To Visit: Reservation confirmed for 6:30pm
Price: yen (affordable, genuinely reasonable per multiple reviews)
Tags: kaiseki; verified via Google Places; affordable; family-run; geographically convenient

Name: Arizuki Ebisu (motsunabe)
Description: Genuine Hakata-style motsunabe (Kyushu offal hot pot), with six soup varieties. ORDER: the signature white miso "Shiro" broth, or the soy-based "Aka" if you prefer something lighter. Typical spend ¥6,000-7,999.
Best Time To Visit: Evening
Tags: motsunabe; hot pot; traditional; verified Tabelog; convenient
Must See Highlight: Try the Shiro (white miso) soup variety
Reservation Info: Reservations accepted starting 2 weeks in advance, online

Name: Manten Sushi Marunouchi
Description: Casual counter omakase 5 minutes from Tokyo Station, tuna sourced from Toyosu. ORDER: the omakase course — let the chef choose. Typical spend ¥10,000-14,999.
Best Time To Visit: 7:00pm - reservation confirmed
Tags: omakase; sushi; verified Google+Tabelog; Top 100 Tabelog

Name: Pontocho Suishin Honten
Description: Casual Kyoto vegetable dishes and obanzai in a traditional machiya. ORDER: seasonal vegetable dishes featuring Kamo eggplant or Manganji peppers, alongside a seafood course. Courses from ¥4,950.
Best Time To Visit: Evening
Tags: vegetables; obanzai; seafood; Tabelog verified; affordable; not kaiseki

Name: Taiyo No To Main Store
Description: Beloved retro Osaka cafe chain, right in Nakazakicho. ORDER: the traditional Japanese breakfast set — simple and satisfying.
Best Time To Visit: Morning

Name: Ueno Station area breakfast
Description: Flexible grab-a-bite stop right at Ueno Station before boarding — bakeries, coffee shops, and casual cafes in the station building. ORDER: whatever pastry or onigiri looks good, or an ekiben if you'd rather eat on the train.
Best Time To Visit: Morning, before your ~10:00am departure (arrives Kanazawa 12:30pm)

Name: Nishi Chaya District (evening walk)
Description: Kanazawa's western geisha district — quieter and more local-feeling than Higashi Chaya. Streets are always open, so this works well as a flexible evening walk whenever you're ready.
Best Time To Visit: Evening

Name: Jukusei Zushi Rita
Description: Aged sushi specialist (jukusei-zushi) - fish dry-aged 6-19 days depending on the cut to concentrate umami, a genuinely distinctive technique. Counter-only, 8 seats. ORDER: the omakase course - aged tuna, aged shima-aji, and aged kanpachi nigiri are specifically praised in reviews.
Tags: aged sushi; omakase; Tabelog verified; counter-only
Reservation Info: Reservation required - fixed seating times only, book in advance

Name: Shibuya Crossing
Hours: Always open, best after dark for the neon effect
Description: The famously chaotic scramble crossing, one of the busiest pedestrian intersections in the world. Whole-group stop on the Day 25 afternoon, after COHINA - about 25 min from Tokyo Station on the JR Yamanote Line. See the crossing, grab photos from the Starbucks second-floor window or the Shibuya Sky observation deck if time allows, then continue on. No need for a long stay to appreciate it.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:45-5:45pm, as it gets dark (dusk is around 5pm in late October). Leave Shibuya by ~6:10pm for the 7:00pm dinner in Marunouchi
Must See Highlight: Watch the crossing from the Starbucks second-floor window across the street

Name: Yayoiken Higashi Ueno
Description: Genuine Japanese teishoku chain, open from 7am - right in Ueno, near your hotel. ORDER: the grilled mackerel set with a tamagoyaki add-on - specifically praised in reviews as an ideal Japanese breakfast. Order via touchscreen kiosk (English available), free rice/tea/pickle refills.
Best Time To Visit: Morning

Name: coffee murasaki
Description: Small, highly regarded coffee stand near Ueno Park. ORDER: their balanced medium-to-dark roast, and try the imagawayaki (red bean pancake sandwich) if you want a little something sweet alongside it.
Best Time To Visit: Morning

Name: Kyoto Station area breakfast
Description: Quick, genuine Japanese breakfast at Kyoto Station between Fushimi Inari and the To-ji market - the goal is a fast refuel, not a long sit-down meal.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:50am, back at Kyoto Station from Inari, before the 15 min walk to To-ji

Name: UNIQLO Shinsaibashisuji Store
Description: Combined Uniqlo and GU store across four floors - Uniqlo on the first two floors, GU on the third and fourth. Note: purchases must be paid separately for Uniqlo and GU items. Tax-free counter available with passport.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:50pm, or after dinner (open to 9pm)

Name: WEGO Shinsaibashi
Description: Affordable Japanese youth/streetwear brand, similar in spirit to Uniqlo but more fashion-forward, with both new items and a curated vintage/used selection mixed in. Popular with younger shoppers.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:30-5:10pm, or after dinner (open to 10pm)

Name: MUJI PARCO Shinsaibashi
Description: Minimalist Japanese lifestyle brand - clothing, stationery, home goods, and snacks all in one. A second opportunity to browse if you want something different from the Ginza location.
Best Time To Visit: ~5:15pm - closes 8pm

Name: ABC-MART Shinsaibashi
Description: Major Japanese shoe/sneaker chain carrying both Japanese and international brands, often with Japan-exclusive colorways not available elsewhere.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:30-5:10pm, or after dinner (open to 9pm)

Name: Enoshima Koya
Description: Ocean-view breakfast spot, open from 8am, expect a short wait even early. ORDER: the Makanai-don (fisherman's breakfast bowl, fish served three ways) or the shirasu-don - both specifically praised in reviews, alongside fresh daily sashimi.
Best Time To Visit: ~10:30am (leave Ueno 9:00am). No weekend reservations for breakfast or lunch, so expect a queue

Name: G★P Coffee Roaster Enoshima
Description: Specialty coffee roaster right in the same area as breakfast. ORDER: the nel drip coffee (Japanese-style pour-over) - specifically recommended in reviews. English menu available.
Best Time To Visit: ~11:25am, right after Koya

Name: Nezu Shrine
Description: One of Tokyo's oldest shrines, famous for its vermillion torii gate tunnel (smaller-scale echo of Fushimi Inari) and, in season, a small azalea garden. Quiet, residential, a natural extension of the Yanaka walk.
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon
Price: Free (small fee for azalea garden in season)
Tags: shrine; torii gates; quiet; adjacent to Yanaka

Name: Ashi Teishoku & Diner
Description: Genuine teishoku diner serving breakfast, lunch, and late-night dining since 2015 (parent cafe in Kuramae since 1974). English-speaking staff. ORDER: one of the daily set meals - vegetable and fish dishes are a specialty.
Best Time To Visit: Morning

Name: M&Maison Kyoto
Description: Renovated traditional Kyoto townhouse, obanzai-style breakfast, 5-minute walk from Gojo Station. ORDER: the one-soup-five-dish set featuring fresh fish of the day (grilled with salt or soy marinade), Omi rice, and seasonal Kyoto vegetables.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - taken off Day 18 on 17 Oct 2026 (breakfast at your stay instead)
Tags: obanzai; Kyoto breakfast; Tabelog verified; Gojo

Name: Tsukiji Honganji Cafe Tsumugi
Description: Famous '18-item breakfast' inside the grounds of Tsukiji Hongan-ji, overlooking the temple's main hall. Placed here on your whole-group day so everyone experiences it before the group splits on Day 26. ORDER: the signature 18-item breakfast set.
Best Time To Visit: Morning
Tags: temple cafe; breakfast; Tabelog verified; Tsukiji
Reservation Info: Online reservation available for breakfast hours

Name: Saiko Shinkan (菜香新館)
Description: Cantonese dim sum specialist across 5 floors, established 1988, selected for Tabelog's Chinese Restaurant Top 100 four separate years. ORDER: their dim sum course - shrimp dumplings and char siu bao are specifically praised. English menu and English/Chinese-speaking staff available.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:45pm, first stop in Chinatown after the Yokohama Station locker - walk-in, expect a Saturday queue; lunch ends 3:30pm
Tags: dim sum; Cantonese; Tabelog verified; Chinatown
Reservation Info: Reservations only accepted for dinner - lunch is walk-in only. Closed Tuesdays.

Name: Coin locker at Yokohama Station (Costco haul)
Description: Drop off Costco purchases in a Large or Extra-Large locker here before continuing to Chinatown sightseeing. Collect on the way back to the hotel at the end of the day. If lockers are full, the ecbo cloak app can reserve storage space at nearby partner locations.

Name: Cup Noodles Museum
Description: Interactive tribute to Momofuku Ando, inventor of instant ramen. Highlight is the 'Make Your Own Cup Noodles' workshop - design your own cup and choose from dozens of soup/topping combinations. Workshop tickets are same-day only and can run out, so by mid-afternoon the workshop may be full - the museum itself is still worth the visit.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:30pm after Chinatown (2 subway stops + walk). Workshop tickets are same-day and may be gone by then on a Saturday; museum closes 6pm, no entry after 5:30pm
Price: yen (500 entry + 500 for the cup noodle workshop)
Must See Highlight: Design and make your own cup noodles to take home
Reservation Info: The My CUPNOODLES Factory workshop cannot be booked: numbered tickets are handed out at the museum on the day, first come first served. Only general admission can be bought online.

Name: Asakusa Station quick breakfast
Hours: From ~6am (convenience store/kiosk hours) - buy the night before if unsure
Description: Grab something quick from a convenience store or station kiosk before the 6:30am Revaty Kegon 1 (arrives Tobu-Nikko 8:25am) - nothing sit-down opens early enough for this departure time. Save the real breakfast experience for after you arrive in Nikko.
Best Time To Visit: By ~6:15am, before the 6:30am train

Name: Haneda Airport - Group Send-off
Description: Whole group travels to Haneda together to see off the early-departure group ahead of their 10am flight - budget arrival by ~8am for check-in/security. Grab breakfast at the airport itself given the early start. Afterward, the remaining group heads to Daikanyama to begin the shopping day: Keikyu to Shinagawa, JR Yamanote to Shibuya, then the Tokyu Toyoko Line one stop to Daikanyama (about 45 min).
Best Time To Visit: Very early morning

Name: Akihabara arcades (late evening only - shops closed by dinner time)
Description: Late-night arcade portion (GiGO, Taito Station, Hey) - all open until ~11pm. Best suited for after dinner, since the retro game shops and Gachapon Kaikan close earlier (7-8pm).
Best Time To Visit: Evening, after dark for the full neon effect
Price: Free to walk around; arcade games are coin-operated

Name: Akimoto (or nearby shirasu-don spot)
Description: Walk-in backup by the station (Tabelog 3.53). Known for tendon (tempura rice bowl) with Kamakura vegetables; also serves shirasu-don, the same whitebait bowl as the Enoshima breakfast, so order the tendon for variety. | Souvenir snack: Dried shirasu (whitebait) packs - Kamakura/Enoshima's local specialty, sold at nearby shops.
Best Time To Visit: If you miss the 2:00pm last order at Grape Republic - last order here is 3:00pm

Name: Kanazawa Rokkaku
Description: Charcoal-grilled yakitori over binchotan, small and intimate. ORDER: a few skewers as a snack rather than a full course - chicken neck meat, thigh, and the grilled rice ball are specifically praised in reviews. Menu has English and Chinese translations.
Best Time To Visit: Evening

Name: Torizune Shizendo (鳥つね自然洞)
Description: Oyakodon (chicken and egg rice bowl) specialist - genuinely different from the teishoku already covered at breakfast. Michelin Bib Gourmand for 8 consecutive years, Tabelog 100 chicken dishes selection, won gold 3 years running in Japan's national oyakodon competition. ORDER: tokujo oyakodon (uses two breeds of free-range chicken). Lunch is casual and affordable despite the prestige - arrive close to open, queues form.
Best Time To Visit: Queue by 11:15am for the 11:30 opening - Ginza Line from Asakusa to Suehirocho is 8 min. Lunch ends 1:30pm, so it has to come before the 2:00pm appointment
Tags: oyakodon; Tabelog verified 3.73; Michelin Bib Gourmand; Ueno area
Reservation Info: No reservations for lunch - arrive early

Name: Shigetsu (inside Tenryu-ji)
Description: Shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) inside Tenryu-ji temple grounds, overlooking the garden. Note: hours are 11am-2pm only - this is lunch, not breakfast. Reservation needed for the mid/top tiers.
Best Time To Visit: Lunch

Name: Aji-Hei (気軽な大衆居酒屋あじ平)
Hours: 17:00-24:00 daily (L.O. 23:00); call ahead on Sundays and holidays (Tabelog, checked 15 Oct 2026)
Description: Genuine Showa-retro local izakaya, 6 min walk from Takayama Station. Broad izakaya menu covering tsukemono steak, hoba miso, and fresh Sea of Japan seafood, alongside local sake. You have hoba miso at Kyouya at lunch, so order the seafood or tsukemono steak here. 80 seats: counter plus tatami rooms on two floors. Casual, welcoming to solo diners and groups, decades of local regulars.
Best Time To Visit: 5:00pm opening - walk-in
Reservation Info: Walk-in - arrive at the 5:00pm opening; you may have to queue. Online booking via Tabelog is possible if you change your mind (the phone line is closed)

Name: Kamakura Chacha (総本家鎌倉茶々)
Description: Matcha soft-serve with 5 adjustable intensity levels, up to Level MAX for serious matcha fans. The definitive local matcha snack on Komachi-dori, using rare stone-ground tea (only 20g/hour). Mini portion, genuinely made for walking and eating.
Best Time To Visit: ~2:40pm, walking back down Komachi-dori to the station after lunch
Tags: matcha; soft serve; walking snack; Komachi-dori

Name: Uiro (ういろう) - Nagoya Station
Description: Steamed rice cake, Nagoya's other famous specialty alongside hitsumabushi - not fried, easy to grab at the station for the train. Individually wrapped pieces sold at station kiosks and depachika, no sit-down needed.
Best Time To Visit: While passing through Nagoya Station
Tags: uiro; Nagoya specialty; steamed; walking snack

Name: Yuba-man (ゆばまん) - Randen Arashiyama Station
Description: Steamed bun filled with seasoned pork and yuba (tofu skin) - a distinctive Arashiyama-only item, different from the matcha desserts everywhere else in the neighborhood. Sold right in the station building, same spot as the Kimono Forest - eat on a bench there.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:45pm, grab one at Randen Arashiyama station on the way out
Tags: yuba; steamed bun; walking snack; Arashiyama station

Name: Tajima beef-man (但馬牛まん)
Description: Steamed bun filled with premium Tajima beef (the regional brand behind Kobe beef) - genuinely local specialty, steamed not fried, grab-and-go format for the morning onsen-town walk before the travel day begins. 5 min walk from Kinosaki Onsen Station.
Best Time To Visit: Morning walk
Tags: Tajima beef; steamed bun; walking snack; Kinosaki

Name: Hagumo (羽雲) - Haneda Airport
Description: Haneda-exclusive dorayaki - fluffy, cloud-like pancake with Hokkaido azuki, less sweet than standard. A fitting final Japan snack before departure - sold at Tokyo Shokuhinkan in both terminals.
Best Time To Visit: Before departure

Name: Fuurainbou tebasaki (風来坊) - Nagoya Station
Description: Tebasaki (fried chicken wings) - Nagoya's single most famous specialty, and Fuurainbou is the actual originator of the dish. Sweet-savory tare glaze, genuinely different from anything else covered on the trip. Dedicated takeout counter in Esca underground mall, easy grab for the train.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:15pm, back at Nagoya Station after the museum, before the ~3:40pm Shinkansen
Tags: tebasaki; Nagoya specialty; fried; walking snack

Name: Tora-hachi (とら八) - late night yakiton
Description: Late-night yakiton (grilled pork skewers) izakaya, 1 minute from Akihabara Station Showa-dori exit. Right where you already are after the arcades - fresh morning-butchered offal, charcoal-grilled. Casual, welcoming to solo diners, multiple floors of seating.
Best Time To Visit: Late evening after the arcades
Tags: yakiton; late night; Akihabara; Tabelog verified 3.42

Name: Izakaya Hanagumi (居酒屋 花組)
Description: Seafood izakaya specializing in Nodoguro (robatayaki-grilled, sashimi, rice dishes) and Kanazawa Oden. Genuine online instant reservation, no phone needed - accepted until 9pm same-day. 5 min walk from Katamachi bus stop. ORDER: the nodoguro course with steamed sushi, or a la carte nodoguro/oden/sashimi platter.
Best Time To Visit: Evening
Tags: nodoguro; Kanazawa oden; Tabelog verified 3.53; online booking

Name: Taishu Kappou Uogin (backup)
Description: Sister restaurant to Hanagumi (same company, same menu/course structure) - nodoguro in multiple styles, Kanazawa oden, sashimi. Genuine online instant reservation.
Best Time To Visit: Evening
Reservation Info: Online instant reservation, no phone needed

Name: Meshiya Gyokaijin Ura Katamachi ten (めしや 魚界人)
Description: Independent robatayaki restaurant - genuine charcoal-grilled nodoguro (whole grilled, stick-seared sushi), extensive Kanazawa oden, Noto beef/pork, Kaga vegetables. Tabelog 3.60. 20+ only - no entry for anyone under 20, even with a guardian. 30 seconds from Katamachi Scramble.
Best Time To Visit: 7:00pm (back in Kanazawa ~6:20pm)
Reservation Info: Online instant reservation, phone for same-day

Name: Rakugan Moroeya Nishichaya Karyo Ajiwai
Description: Historic rakugan (dried sugar candy) specialist with a tea room, right in the Nishi Chaya District. Tabelog 100 WEST 2023 selection. IMPORTANT: closes 5pm - visit before or during the Nishi Chaya walk, not after, since this closes earlier than a typical evening stroll.
Best Time To Visit: By ~4:15pm - closes 5pm. About 10-12 min by taxi from Higashi Chaya
Tags: rakugan; wagashi; Nishi Chaya; Tabelog verified 3.66

Name: Osaka Naniwaya
Hours: Mon/Tue/Fri 12:00-21:00; Sat 11:00-21:00; Sun/holidays 11:00-18:00 (last order 15 min before close); closed Wed/Thu (Tabelog, checked 13 Oct 2026)
Description: Taiyaki and kakigori specialist, Tabelog 100 selection for FIVE separate years (2018, 2019, 2020, 2022, 2023) - genuinely sustained excellence. Near the north end of Tenjinbashisuji, the last stop before heading south to Shinsaibashi. Only taiyaki can be reserved - seats and kakigori are first-come.
Best Time To Visit: ~2:40pm, about 10 min walk west from Nikugoro - dessert after the yakiniku. Opens 12:00 on Tuesdays
Reservation Info: Taiyaki only can be reserved by phone

Name: GOOD NEWS TOKYO (Tokyo Station)
Description: Butter sandwich (Butter's Cousin) specialty shop right inside Tokyo Station itself - a currently trendy confection, genuinely distinct from anything else covered. Easy grab near the Kit Kat Chocolatory.
Best Time To Visit: On the way through Tokyo Station on arrival
Tags: butter sandwich; Tokyo Station; Tabelog verified 3.44

Name: Asakusa evening walk (Nakamise/Kaminarimon illuminated)
Description: A general evening walk through Asakusa after dinner - Kaminarimon gate and the Nakamise approach are both illuminated at night, a different atmosphere from daytime.
Best Time To Visit: After dinner

Name: Ueno Land (gachapon)
Description: Gachapon (capsule toy) corner right inside Ueno Station itself, 3rd floor near the Keihin-Tohoku Line platforms. Panda-themed exclusives make a nice Ueno-specific souvenir. Zero detour needed since you are staying in Ueno - easy to duck into anytime passing through the station.
Best Time To Visit: Anytime while passing through Ueno Station

Name: Hoppy Street (ホッピー通り)
Hours: Most shops open afternoon into late evening
Description: An 80-meter alley of retro Showa-era izakaya stalls just behind Senso-ji, reached via Denbo-in-dori (a different lane from Nakamise). Open-fronted tables spill into the street, red lanterns, locals and regulars mixed with visitors. Specialty is gyusuji-nikomi (slow-simmered beef tendon stew) with Hoppy, a beer-like drink mixed with shochu. A genuine old-Tokyo drinking-alley experience, distinct from the Nakamise souvenir walk.
Best Time To Visit: Afternoon into evening
Tags: retro izakaya alley; local; Showa atmosphere; Asakusa
Reservation Info: Walk-in, some shops no reservation possible

Name: Funabashi-dori Shotengai (船橋通り商店街)
Description: A genuinely quiet, local shopping street near Naramachi - used to be busy around a train station that closed in 1969, and has kept its own unhurried character since. Old-fashioned bakeries, retro cafes in renovated old buildings, small independent bookshops, and an onigiri specialty shop. A different pace from the touristy Kintetsu Nara Station area.
Best Time To Visit: Daytime
Tags: local shopping street; retro; Naramachi area; hidden gem

Name: Onari-dori (御成通り)
Description: A genuinely quiet, local shopping street on the West Exit of Kamakura Station - directly opposite Komachi-dori and Tsurugaoka Hachimangu (East Exit). Young locals call it Ura-Kama (the other side of Kamakura). Showa-retro atmosphere, local cafes, bakeries, and zakka shops, distinctly less touristy than Komachi-dori.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:10pm, a short walk-through after TUZURU. Skip it if you are running late for Iwata Coffee
Tags: local shopping street; quiet; Kamakura Station West Exit

Name: Honmachi-dori (本町通り)
Neighborhood: Along the Miyagawa river, station side
Description: Explicitly called Takayama citizens kitchen by locals - genuine everyday shops (clothing, household goods), quieter than Sanmachi across the river. The actual real-world setting used in the anime Hyouka.
Best Time To Visit: ~10:30am, walking north along the river toward Kyouya

Name: Kokubunji-dori Shotengai (国分寺通り商店街)
Neighborhood: Near Takayama Station, in front of Hida Kokubunji
Description: 2-3 min walk from Takayama Station, in front of Hida Kokubunji temple. Reviewers explicitly note almost no tourists here - local eateries rather than souvenir shops, with a few genuine finds like Hida beef nigiri.
Best Time To Visit: ~10:05am, about 8 min walk west from Jinya Dango
Tags: local shopping street; quiet; near station

Name: Sanjokai Shotengai (三条会商店街)
Description: An 800-meter covered arcade near Nijo Castle, genuine daily-life character - locals buying dinner ingredients, mixed with newer cafes. Try Sweets Cafe KYOTO KEIZOs 10-minute Mont Blanc - must be eaten within 10 minutes of serving for the best texture.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - best late afternoon, when locals shop for dinner
Tags: local shopping arcade; near Nijo Castle; unique sweet

Name: Karahori Shotengai (空堀商店街)
Hours: Early morning is quietest and most authentic
Description: Genuinely retains old Osaka shitamachi character - a 100+ year old tofu shop still selling fresh yuba (sells out early), backstreets lined with century-old nagaya row houses. A real residential feel, not built for visitors. Locals recommend early morning for the most authentic experience.
Best Time To Visit: ~10:30-11:00am, before the old tofu shop's yuba sells out. About 20 min on foot east from Kuromon
Tags: old shitamachi; local shopping street; quiet

Name: Motomachi's backstreets
Description: Yokohama's own official tourism site recommends the backstreets behind the main Motomachi Shopping Street specifically - stylish cafes, individual zakka shops, well-regarded restaurants, a quieter counterpoint to Chinatown's crowds right next door. Same station (Motomachi-Chukagai).
Best Time To Visit: Daytime

Name: Sakai Kokodo Ukiyo-e (酒井好古堂)
Description: Genuinely affordable ukiyo-e prints - postcards, reproductions, and reprints starting from a few hundred yen, alongside pricier originals if you want something more serious. Two locations in the immediate area (Nakamise-dori and Denbo-in-dori) with slightly different stock, worth checking both if time allows. Right on your existing walking path.
Best Time To Visit: Daytime
Price: yen (very affordable for reproductions, up to significant for originals)

Name: GU Okachimachi
Description: UNIQLOs affordable fast-fashion sister brand, genuinely close to Ameyoko/Ueno.
Best Time To Visit: Daytime

Name: Welcia Ueno/Okachimachi
Hours: Some locations 24 hours, check nearest branch
Description: Skincare and drugstore chain, multiple branches in the Ueno/Okachimachi area, some genuinely 24-hour. Good alongside Matsumoto Kiyoshi for comparing skincare prices/selection.
Best Time To Visit: Anytime, check nearest branch hours

Name: Hands Shibuya (main store)
Description: The original Hands flagship: split-level floors with multi-brand stationery (pens, notebooks, paper, desk goods) alongside tools, crafts and lifestyle goods - a one-stop shop for stationery brands. Closing for good on 15 Nov 2026 when its lease ends.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:25-5:15pm: JR Harajuku to Shibuya (one stop), then ~8 min walk
Tags: stationery; multi-brand; lifestyle goods; closing Nov 2026

Name: Don Quijote Shinjuku Higashiguchi Honten
Description: The original, historically iconic Don Quijote flagship, genuinely 24-hour, 5 min from Shinjuku Station in Kabuki-cho. About 15 min from Tokyo Station on the JR Chuo Line rapid, so from your Tokyo Station hotel it is a separate trip, not on the way. Cosmetics/snacks on 1F, daily goods 2F, electronics 3F, plus cosplay and souvenir items throughout.
Best Time To Visit: After dinner, straight after the 3D cat screen - open 24 hours, so there is no rush. If you are tired after the journey, both can slide to late on Day 24
Tags: discount variety store; Don Quijote; 24 hour

Name: 3COINS Ecute Ueno
Description: Affordable variety/accessory store (most items 300 yen), located right inside Ueno Station itself.
Best Time To Visit: Anytime

Name: Teramachi & Shinkyogoku Arcades
Description: Two connected covered arcades, directly adjacent to Nishiki Market, a few minutes walk from Pontocho where your dinner already is. Genuinely unique finds not covered elsewhere: POKER FACE (eyewear specialist), The REAL McCOYS (famous vintage Americana), Roeco by Jam (vintage/import fashion), Mishima-tei (historic sukiyaki since the Meiji era). Also has snack stalls (crepes, Taiwanese castella) if you want a walking treat after dinner.
Best Time To Visit: Evening, after dinner
Tags: shopping arcade; near Pontocho; unique shops

Name: Kinako to Torori (きなことろり)
Description: Warabi mochi specialty shop by the established Kisho Karyo brand, dedicated to showcasing deep-roasted kinako as the star ingredient. Fresh warabi mochi made daily, wrapped by hand in house-roasted kinako - a genuine snack, not a drink.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:45pm, a few minutes from Tsujiri - hours not confirmed

Name: Nakamura Tokichi Honten (中村藤吉本店)
Description: Founded 1854, 170+ years - one of the two most famous names (alongside Ito Kyuemon) in spreading Uji tea nationally. Tabelog 3.55, selected for the West 100 Japanese sweets list 2023. ORDER: nama-cha jelly (genuinely unusual to find hojicha wagashi, not just matcha) - a real snack format. Right on Ujibashi-dori, the same street connecting Uji Station to Byodo-in, so this needs zero detour from your existing route.
Best Time To Visit: Daytime
Tags: genmaicha; hojicha; tea snacks; Uji specialist

Name: Tsujirihei Honten (辻利兵衛本店)
Description: Right on Ujibashi-dori. ORDER specifically these souvenir items: Uji matcha nama dorayaki Doosenbo (宇治抹茶生どら焼き 童仙房), Kyo matcha Take Baumkuchen (京抹茶「竹」バウム), and the 3-flavor langue de chat set (宇治茶三種お濃いくちラングドシャ茶賓 - matcha/hojicha/genmaicha). Tabelog 3.30.
Best Time To Visit: Same visit as Nakamura Tokichi
Tags: souvenirs; genmaicha; hojicha; Uji tea specialist

Name: Kamigata Ukiyo-e Museum (printing experience)
Description: Genuine, currently-operating ukiyo-e printing workshop. 3 course levels: Beginner (1,000 yen, 30 min, 3-color), Intermediate (1,500 yen, 30-45 min, 4-color, design features Hozenji Yokocho), Advanced (1,800 yen, 45-60 min). Book via Jalan: https://www.jalan.net/kankou/spt_27128ae3302028721/activity/l0000396DA/ - or call 06-6211-0303. English page available.
Best Time To Visit: Optional: ~4:30-5:15pm, right before the 6:00pm dinner 3 min away (last entry 5:30pm). Needs booking 3 days ahead
Price: yen (1,000-1,800 for the printing experience, plus museum admission)
Tags: woodblock printing; ukiyo-e; craft workshop; genuine booking via Jalan
Reservation Info: Book via Jalan link above, or phone 06-6211-0303, or contact form. 3 days advance notice required.
Source: Verified directly via official site and Jalan

Name: Dotonbori Jihei (道頓堀治兵衛)
Hours: Check current hours, lunch and dinner service
Description: Fugu specialist, 2 min walk from Namba Station Exit 25, right in Dotonbori. Tabelog 3.38 - genuine, legally licensed operation (fugu handling is strictly regulated by law across Japan, requiring certified staff). Score reflects casual/value positioning, not safety concerns. ORDER: the seasonal Cosmos course (秋桜) - explicitly combines fugu hot pot with matsutake dobin-mushi, matching what drew you to Yanaka no Suzume originally. Genuine online reservation available. River-view seating popular.
Tags: fugu; matsutake; Dotonbori; Tabelog verified 3.38; online booking

Name: Nezu Kamachiku (根津釜竹)
Hours: 11:30am-2:30pm, 5:30pm-9pm approx, closed Sun evening and Mon
Description: Small family-run udon specialist (father-son operation originally from Habikino, Osaka; opened in Tokyo 2005), housed in a beautiful Kuma Kengo-designed building built around a 1910 stone sake warehouse. Tabelog 3.66 (1,300+ reviews), Tabelog 100 Udon EAST 2024 selection. Genuine online instant reservation, no phone needed. ORDER: kamaage udon (hot, in its cooking water) or zaru udon (cold, dipping style) - the menu is intentionally simple, with the focus entirely on noodle quality. Good izakaya-style side dishes and sake list too.
Best Time To Visit: Evening, book ahead given genuine popularity
Tags: udon; small family-run; Tabelog 100; Nezu; genuine online booking

Name: JINS Atre Ueno (eye exam + glasses)
Neighborhood: Inside Atre Ueno, right at Ueno Station
Description: Free eye exam, no doctor visit or prescription needed - standard single-vision glasses ready in as little as 30 minutes. JINS explicitly confirms English-speaking staff and that not speaking Japanese is no barrier. Scheduled for the Day 11 evening (Sun 11 Oct), on the way back from Kamakura and before dinner. This is your last evening in Ueno - the train to Kanazawa leaves ~10:00am on Day 12, when the shop only opens - so choose lenses that can be made the same evening. FALLBACK: if they are not ready before the 9:00pm close, collect them on Day 25 (from Ginza, about 12 min to Ueno on the Ginza Line) or the Day 27 morning from 10am - tell the counter your pickup date and ask how long they hold an order. Note: this is the full-service Atre Ueno location, not the smaller ecute Ueno store inside the ticket gates, which ships glasses later rather than same-day.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00-8:00pm, straight off the train from Kamakura (Ueno ~6:50pm). Order by ~8:00pm at the latest - the shop closes at 9:00pm. Dinner follows at ~8:15pm at Tori no Ichi (about 5 min walk)
Tags: eye exam; glasses; English-speaking staff; same-day
Reservation Info: Walk-in, take a number at the counter
Source: Verified via official JINS site and multiple travel guides

Name: Seijo Ishii Atre Ueno
Neighborhood: Inside Atre Ueno, JR Ueno Station Shinobazu exit
Description: Upscale grocery right inside Ueno Station, 1 min from the Shinobazu exit. Good prepared food options (bento, deli, pastries), not just raw groceries. Open until 11pm.
Best Time To Visit: Alternative to a sit-down dinner, if you want something quick after arriving back from Nikko
Tags: supermarket; late-night option; inside Ueno Station

Name: Maruetsu Higashi-Ueno
Description: Genuinely 24-hour supermarket, ~500m from Ueno Station. The safest late-night option regardless of what time you actually get back.
Best Time To Visit: Anytime, 24 hours

Name: Maruetsu Petit Higashi-Nippori
Description: Genuinely 24-hour supermarket, east of Ueno toward Uguisudani/Higashi-Nippori - a good option if your accommodation is on that side.
Best Time To Visit: Anytime, 24 hours

Name: Maibasuke Taito Shitaya 1-chome
Description: Convenient compact supermarket near Iriya, open until midnight - another east-side option if your accommodation is in that direction.
Best Time To Visit: Anytime until midnight

Name: Inoue
Description: Cafe in Tamakuracho, Nakagyo Ward, near Karasuma Oike.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - taken off Day 18 on 17 Oct 2026

Name: Matsumoto Kiyoshi Echika Fit Ueno (drugstore)
Neighborhood: Inside Tokyo Metro Ueno Station (Ginza/Hibiya line concourse)
Hours: Approx. 7:30am-10pm weekdays (Oct 8 is a Thursday) - verify on arrival
Description: Arrival-day drugstore run. Inside the Tokyo Metro Ueno station concourse, so it fits naturally between Ueno Land and dinner. Pick up toiletries, cold medicine, eye drops, masks, etc. If it is crowded or short on stock, the Ameyoko drugstores just outside (and the Matsumoto Kiyoshi already on Day 9) are backups. Tax-free with passport over 5,000 yen.
Best Time To Visit: ~5:00-5:30pm, before dinner
Tags: drugstore; arrival day; Ueno Station; tax-free

Name: Maruetsu Higashi-Ueno (24h supermarket)
Description: End-of-night grocery stop on the walk home east of Ueno Station. Open 24 hours, so there is no rush after Akihabara/Tora-hachi - take the JR Yamanote/Keihin-Tohoku or Hibiya Line back to Ueno and walk ~5-7 min east. Good for breakfast items, water, fruit, drinks and snacks for the room. Prepared foods (bento, sushi) get discounted stickers late at night.
Best Time To Visit: Last stop of the night, on the way back to the accommodation

Name: Maibasuke Taito Shitaya 1-chome (supermarket)
Description: Alternative to Maruetsu if the accommodation is further north-east toward Iriya. Small AEON-affiliated mini-supermarket, cheaper than a convenience store. Closes at midnight - go to Maruetsu instead if you are running later.
Best Time To Visit: Before midnight

Name: Maruetsu Petit Higashi-Nippori (24h supermarket)
Description: Alternative 24-hour option if the accommodation is further north toward Uguisudani/Nippori. Smaller than the Higashi-Ueno Maruetsu.
Best Time To Visit: Anytime late

Name: SOU・SOU (Shinkyogoku flagship shops)
Description: About nine small SOU・SOU shops clustered on Shinkyogoku-dori: Kikoromo (women's Japanese wear), Tabi (jika-tabi shoes), Isemomen (Ise cotton), Hotei (bags/textiles), Yousou. (western basics that pair with the Japanese pieces). On Day 18 it is a 5-10 min walk from the Pontocho dinner and sits in the same arcades as the Teramachi & Shinkyogoku stop.
Best Time To Visit: ~4:30-5:45pm: taxi from Ginkaku-ji (~20 min, ~¥2,000 - Sunday buses are packed). Closes 8pm; 5-10 min walk to the 6:15pm dinner
Tags: shopping; SOU・SOU; tabi; textiles; texture and design

Name: Nakagawa Masashichi Shoten (LAQUE Shijo Karasuma)
Description: Lifestyle goods from the 300-year-old Nara textile house: linen and hemp cloths, kitchen tools, apparel, travel pouches. Close to Nakashimaya (about 5-10 min walk to dinner). Tax-free with passport.
Best Time To Visit: ~5:50-6:20pm, right before the 6:30pm Nakashimaya dinner. Subway from Nijojo-mae, about 15 min
Tags: shopping; Nakagawa Masashichi; crafts; texture and design

Name: Namba Parks: nest Robe + Nakagawa Masashichi
Description: Two stops in one building: nest Robe / CONFECT (3F) - natural linen and cotton womenswear, and the branch that carries UpcycleLino, their line remade from used linen - plus Nakagawa Masashichi Shoten (5F). Floors checked on the Namba Parks floor map, 13 Oct 2026. If time allows: RAGTAG (4F, secondhand) and Yuzawaya (5F, craft supplies). About 10 minutes' walk south of Dotonbori, where dinner follows.
Best Time To Visit: ~5:50-6:30pm, about 15 min walk south from Shinsaibashi - shops open to ~9pm
Tags: shopping; nest Robe; Nakagawa Masashichi; feminine natural; linen

Name: COHINA Store (Shibuya Hikarie ShinQs 4F)
Neighborhood: Shibuya Hikarie, east side of Shibuya Station
Description: COHINA's permanent Tokyo store: clothing cut for women around 155cm and under, including their denim. Inside Hikarie, directly connected to Shibuya Station - a minute from the crossing. Oct 25 is a Sunday, open until 8pm.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:45pm, after dropping the Ginza bags at your stay (Tokyo Station to Shibuya is about 25 min on the JR Yamanote Line) - closes 8pm on Sundays
Tags: shopping; COHINA; denim; petite; feminine natural

Name: KITTE Marunouchi: Nakagawa Masashichi (4F) + GOOD DESIGN STORE (3F, MONPE)
Neighborhood: KITTE, next to Tokyo Station Marunouchi South Exit
Description: Two picks in one building beside Tokyo Station. 4F: Nakagawa Masashichi Shoten (linen, household goods, apparel). 3F: GOOD DESIGN STORE TOKYO by NOHARA, which sells Unagi no Nedoko MONPE trousers - stock varies, so check the sizes/fabrics you want are there. Both close at 8pm.
Best Time To Visit: After the Daimaru food hall on arrival, ~5:15-6:15pm with the 10:34am train from Kinosaki - closes 8pm
Tags: shopping; Nakagawa Masashichi; MONPE; texture and design; Tokyo Station

Name: iki ESPRESSO
Description: New Zealand-style cafe in Tokyo's coffee district, Tabelog 3.59 (1,400+ reviews) - flat whites and a proper sit-down brunch-style breakfast. It's one of the few good options open at 8am on a Sunday in this area (the Monzen-nakacho cafes open at 9-10am). CARD/PAYPAY ONLY - no cash. From here it's one stop on the Toei Oedo Line (Kiyosumi-shirakawa to Monzen-nakacho) or a ~20 min walk to the antique market.
Best Time To Visit: 8:00am opening - aim to leave by ~8:30

Name: Tomioka Hachimangu Antique Market
Hours: 6:00am-5:00pm on the 1st (not Jan), 2nd, 4th and 5th Sundays - Oct 25 is the 4th Sunday
Description: Long-running outdoor antique and flea market in the grounds of Tomioka Hachimangu shrine: vintage kimono and fabric, ceramics, old tools, prints and small curios. Plan it in two passes around the fire ritual next door - a first look from ~8:45 before the 9:00 ritual (early is when dealers put out their best pieces), then back from ~9:30 until ~10:40. Bring cash; most stalls don't take cards. Dates can change without notice - check @tomioka_antiquemarket on Instagram the week before.
Tags: antiques; flea market; vintage kimono; ceramics; secondhand; cash only

Name: Fukagawa Fudo-do Fire Ritual (Goma)
Description: Free to watch: monks burn wooden prayer sticks in a large fire while chanting sutras, backed by taiko drums billed as the largest in Japan - loud and dramatic. About a 2-3 minute walk from the antique market. You don't need to stay for the whole ceremony: arrive a few minutes early, sit or stand near the back, and leave quietly between chants. No photos or video in the main hall during the ritual (check signs on arrival). 15-20 minutes is enough to see the fire and hear the drums.
Best Time To Visit: 9:00am ritual
Tags: temple; fire ritual; taiko; free; cultural

Name: Tokyo Station breakfast (backup)
Hours: Sunday openings: Hatsufuji 7:00; Rokurinsha & Tamejiro 7:30; Mango Tree Gapao & Sushiko Nagomi 8:00
Description: Backup if you'd rather eat near the hotel before heading out (Tozai Line from Nihonbashi or Otemachi to Monzen-nakacho, ~15 min door to door). All outside the JR ticket gates, all open early on Sunday: (1) Rokurinsha, Tokyo Ramen Street B1F - morning tsukemen (dipping noodles) ¥790, 7:30-9:45, Tabelog 3.77 and Tabelog top-100 ramen; queues, so arrive at 7:30. (2) Soba Tamejiro, Ichibangai 1F - soba/udon morning sets, 7:30, Tabelog 3.49, Suica/IC only. (3) Yaesu Hatsufuji, Yaesu underground - grilled fish breakfast set, 7:00, Tabelog 3.49. (4) Mango Tree Kitchen Gapao, Gransta Marunouchi B1F - Thai congee or gapao rice, 8:00, Tabelog 3.33. (5) Tsukiji Sushiko Nagomi, Gransta Marunouchi B1F - sushi / sea bream ochazuke, 8:00 on Sundays, Tabelog 3.32. None serve specialty coffee.
Best Time To Visit: 7:00-8:00am, then Tozai Line to Monzen-nakacho
Tags: breakfast; backup; Tokyo Station; Japanese; Asian

Name: MONZ CAFE (coffee backup)
Neighborhood: Monzen-nakacho, on the Fukagawa Fudo-do temple approach
Description: Coffee backup right at the market: sits on the approach street to Fukagawa Fudo-do, 1 min from Monzen-nakacho Exit 1, Tabelog 3.57 (660+ reviews). Opens at 9:00, so it's too late for the pre-ritual breakfast but ideal for a coffee between the 9:00 fire ritual and your second pass through the antique market. Small (18 seats, some on a terrace); takeout works too. Cards and mobile payment accepted. Known for seasonal baked cakes.
Best Time To Visit: ~9:20am, right after the fire ritual

Name: Ponta Honke (pork cutlet)
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION. The original Japanese pork katsuretsu, served since 1905 - thin golden crust, very tender loin. Tabelog 3.76 (2,000+ reviews), Tabelog top-100 for Japanese-style Western food 2025. Closest of the sit-down options to your stay. Last order is 7:45pm, so don't arrive after ~7:15.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)
Reservation Info: Reservations accepted for 2+ by phone (03-3831-2351); walk-in also possible

Name: Yonekyu Honten (beef hotpot)
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION. Gyunabe - the Meiji-era beef hotpot that sukiyaki grew out of - served since 1886 in an old wooden house; a drum is struck as you walk in. Tabelog 3.65 (1,300 reviews), Tabelog top-100 hotpot 2024. The most atmospheric of the options.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)
Tags: dinner option; gyunabe; sukiyaki; hotpot; Tabelog 100
Reservation Info: Walk-in only (bookings only for groups of 10+)

Name: Komagata Dozeu (loach hotpot)
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION. Dozeu nabe - small whole loach simmered in a shallow iron pot under a mountain of green onion - served since 1801, floor seating in an Edo-style hall. Tabelog 3.59 (2,000+ reviews). Closes at 8pm, so 7pm is tight - go by 6:30.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)
Tags: dinner option; dozeu; Edo food; hotpot

Name: Asakusa Gyukatsu (beef cutlet)
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION. Gyukatsu - breaded beef cutlet fried rare that you finish on a hot stone at your seat. Tabelog 3.45 (380 reviews), the best-rated gyukatsu near you. 20 counter seats, queues at peak times. Quick and inexpensive. Takes cards.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)
Tags: dinner option; gyukatsu; beef cutlet; casual

Name: Men Mitsui (ramen)
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION. The best bowl near you: refined soy-sauce ramen with hand-kneaded noodles. Tabelog 3.83 (1,580 reviews), Tabelog top-100 ramen 2024 and 2025. 11 counter seats. CATCH: you must collect a timed ticket in person at the shop from 5:30pm, then come back at your slot.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)
Reservation Info: Timed tickets handed out at the shop from 5:30pm for dinner

Name: Menya Haru (ramen)
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION. Rich, deep broth that changes daily. Tabelog 3.79 (2,670 reviews), Tabelog top-100 ramen 8 years running. Only 7 counter seats - just join the queue. Cash only. The heavier style of ramen.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)
Tags: dinner option; ramen; Tabelog 100; cash only

Name: Shina Soba Yamato Inaricho (ramen)
Neighborhood: Inaricho, east of Ueno - closest ramen to your stay
Hours: Wed-Sat 11:30am-3:30pm, 5:00-9:00pm; Tue/Sun lunch only; closed Mondays
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION. Clear soy-sauce broth with wontons and thin noodles - a light bowl, 2 minutes from Inaricho Station and on your way home. Tabelog 3.74 (1,050 reviews). Cash or PayPay.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)

Name: Ramen Kamo to Negi (duck ramen)
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION - also works late at night after Akihabara. Duck ramen made from just duck, leek and water, plus a popular duck-and-egg rice bowl. Tabelog 3.73 (4,800 reviews). Often long queues. Cash only.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)
Tags: dinner option; ramen; duck; late night; cash only

Name: Toriton (conveyor-belt sushi, Tokyo Solamachi)
Neighborhood: Oshiage, base of Tokyo Skytree - 2 stops from Asakusa
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION. Popular Hokkaido conveyor-belt sushi chain with very fresh fish, on the 6th floor of the mall under Tokyo Skytree (lit up at night). Tabelog 3.46 (1,200 reviews) - the best-rated conveyor-belt sushi near you. Register your phone at the machine and browse the mall until you get a text; weekday waits are usually 20-40 minutes.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)
Reservation Info: No reservations - numbered ticket with phone notification

Name: Miura Misaki Port Ueno (conveyor-belt sushi)
Neighborhood: Ueno, ~5 min from JR Ueno Station
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION. Conveyor-belt sushi run by a tuna wholesaler from Misaki port - the best fish of the budget sushi places here. Signature: a heaped chutoro (fatty tuna) gunkan for about 110 yen. Tabelog 3.27 (380 reviews).
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)
Tags: dinner option; conveyor-belt sushi; tuna; budget

Name: Genki Sushi x Uobei Ueno (tablet-order sushi)
Neighborhood: Ueno Gate building 3F, ~3 min from JR Ueno Station
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION. The two brands' first joint flagship (opened Oct 2025). No rotating belt: order on a tablet and plates shoot to your seat on a high-speed lane, plus a rotating 'world sushi' fusion menu. 58 counter seats. Fun and easy for first-timers; too new for a meaningful Tabelog score.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)
Reservation Info: Join the queue in the Club Genki app, or walk in

Name: Sushiro (Ueno or Asakusa Rokku)
Neighborhood: Ueno: ~3 min from Keisei-Ueno. Asakusa Rokku: ~1 min from Asakusa (TX) Station
Hours: Check the Sushiro app for the branch hours on the day
Description: DAY 8 CASUAL DINNER OPTION. Japan's biggest budget sushi chain - plates from about 120 yen, English touch-screen ordering, plates arrive on a fast lane. Tabelog ~3.1 at both branches: go for the fun and the price, not the fish. Book a table or join the queue in the Sushiro app to avoid the 7pm wait.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8)
Reservation Info: Reserve or queue in the Sushiro app

Name: Appointment near JR Okachimachi Station (2:00pm)
Description: Your 1-hour appointment, booked for 2:00pm. Aim to be at JR Okachimachi Station by 1:45. From Kakimori: Oedo Line from Kuramae to Ueno-Okachimachi (2 stops) or a ~15 min walk. Treat 1:20pm as the latest time to leave Kakimori; if the notebook isn't ready, come back for it later (open until 6pm). Afterwards you're at the south end of Ameyoko - walk north through it to Ueno Station.
Best Time To Visit: Arrive by 1:45pm

Name: Kanazawa Crafts Hirosaka
Hours: 10:00-18:00; closed Mondays, or the next day when Monday is a holiday (so open Mon 12 Oct, closed Tue 13 Oct)
Description: A genuine one-stop shop for Kanazawa's lesser-known crafts beyond gold leaf - Kaga embroidery (Kaga-nui), Kaga fishing flies, Futamata Japanese paper, paulownia woodcraft, wagasa (bamboo-and-paper umbrellas), and Kaga mizuhiki gift-wrapping strings. Right near Kenroku-en.
Best Time To Visit: ~5:00-5:40pm, after Nishi Chaya and before the 6:15pm dinner at Hanagumi (3-4 min walk) - closes 6pm
Tags: crafts; Kaga embroidery; paulownia; umbrellas; convenient

Name: Grape Republic Vineria Salone
Neighborhood: Komachi, 7 min walk from Kamakura Station (toward Tsurugaoka Hachimangu)
Description: Italian lunch on a side street off Komachi-dori, run by a Yamagata natural-wine maker. ORDER: the lunch pasta set or the house lasagna. Tabelog 3.70 (500 reviews). The only Italian meal on the trip.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:30pm, straight from the Enoden at Kamakura Station (7 min walk). Last order 2:00pm, so do not let the morning run late
Tags: Italian; pasta; Tabelog verified 3.70; bookable online
Reservation Info: Not booked yet - online booking via Tabelog, or phone 050-5594-2569. Sunday of a holiday weekend, so book

Name: Coffee House Maki
Neighborhood: Demachi (Kawaramachi-Imadegawa), 3 min walk from Demachi Futaba
Hours: 8:30-19:00, no regular closed day (from a 3rd-party article - not confirmed on an official page)
Description: Long-running neighbourhood kissaten by the Kamo River. ORDER: the morning set (about 650 yen) - thick toast hollowed into a box and filled with salad, potato salad, ham and egg - with a coffee. Served until noon.
Best Time To Visit: ~8:45am - leave your stay by 8:15 (subway north to Imadegawa, then a 10 min walk east)

Name: Renkon (lotus-root izakaya)
Neighborhood: Ueno, 3 min from JR Ueno Station - close to your stay
Description: DAY 8 DINNER PICK. Lotus-root specialist with about 20 lotus-root dishes plus other creative Japanese plates - vegetable-led, with fish and chicken alongside. ORDER: the lotus root and shrimp sandwich-fry and the large steamed shumai; choose the steamed and simmered dishes for a lighter meal. Tabelog 3.53 (1,084 reviews). 111 seats over three floors and open late, so it suits an arrival night with an uncertain time.
Best Time To Visit: ~7:00pm (Thu Oct 8), after dropping bags
Tags: dinner pick; lotus root; vegetables; izakaya; near stay
Reservation Info: Not booked yet - online via Tabelog or phone 050-5872-2235. Walk-in is possible but it gets crowded

Name: Awa Naramachi (粟 ならまち店)
Neighborhood: Naramachi, about 15 min walk from Kintetsu Nara Station
Description: DAY 21 DINNER. Course meals built on traditional Yamato (Nara) heirloom vegetables, with a steamed pot and grilled meat, in a 140-year-old Naramachi townhouse. Tabelog 3.64 (365 reviews). Vegetable-led, and five minutes from where the Nara walk ends. Trains back to Kyoto run until about 11pm (JR ~45-70 min, Kintetsu ~50 min), so a 5:30pm dinner gets you back around 9pm.
Best Time To Visit: 5:30pm opening, after Naramachi; leave Nara by ~8:00pm
Tags: dinner; Yamato vegetables; townhouse; Tabelog verified 3.64
Reservation Info: Not booked yet - reservation only, by phone 0742-24-5699

Name: Tempura Tokoro Kyorinsen
Hours: Lunch 11:30-14:00 L.O.; dinner 17:00-22:00 (food L.O. 21:00); closed Mondays
Description: Directly connected to Kyoto Station, operated by the Michelin two-star restaurant Sansou Kyoyamato. Uses a specific blend of light 'Shiro-mon oil' with sesame oil, explicitly designed to be lighter and avoid the heaviness of typical Kanto-style tempura - a genuine fix for anyone who finds standard Tokyo tempura too dark/oily. Features seasonal Kyoto vegetables. Tabelog 3.66. Day 21 dinner backup, eaten after the train back from Nara.
Best Time To Visit: Backup dinner if Awa Naramachi cannot seat you: eat here on arrival back at Kyoto Station, ~7:00-8:30pm
Tags: tempura; light oil; Michelin-affiliated; Kyoto vegetables; convenient
Reservation Info: Dinner reservations accepted online (Tabelog) or phone 050-3628-7377. Only book if Awa falls through

Name: Hachidaime Gihey (八代目儀兵衛)
Hours: Daily 8:00-15:00 (L.O. 14:30); dinner Fri-Sun 17:00-20:00; irregular closed days (Tabelog, checked 17 Oct 2026)
Description: A rice specialist run by an eighth-generation Kyoto rice merchant: rice cooked to order in clay pots is the main event, served as a set with grilled fish (black cod) or wagyu sukiyaki and side dishes. Tabelog 3.56 (952 reviews). Seatings are 50 minutes and you pre-order on arrival, so it keeps the day moving.
Best Time To Visit: Not scheduled - taken off Day 18 on 17 Oct 2026
Tags: lunch; rice; clay pot; Gion; Tabelog verified 3.56
Reservation Info: Not booked. Online via Tabelog; same-day lunch bookings are not taken by phone. Arrive 10 min before the booking

Name: Kotori (鎌倉・文具と雑貨の店 コトリ)
Neighborhood: Omachi, 7 min walk from Kamakura Station East Exit
Hours: Tue-Sun 11:00-18:00; Mon 11:00-17:00 (irregular closed days, sometimes Mondays)
Description: Small stationery and zakka shop with its own designs: pen cases, masking tape, goshuin books and tenugui, plus a shop stamp and postcards. It sits among houses in Omachi, not on a shopping street, so it is a there-and-back detour from the station.
Best Time To Visit: ~5:05pm, a 10 min walk south from Iwata Coffee - closes 6:00pm. Then back to the station for the ~5:40pm train to Ueno

Name: TUZURU
Neighborhood: Onarimachi, 2 min walk from Kamakura Station West Exit
Description: Stationery select shop in a small detached house by the railway line: fountain pens, ink, letter paper, washi tape, and Kamakura postcards and tote bags. No photos inside. Onari-dori is right beside it.
Best Time To Visit: ~3:57pm, straight off the Enoden (West Exit side) - closes 5:00pm

Name: 3COINS+plus Nishi-Ginza
Description: One of the biggest 3COINS branches (billed as the largest in the Kanto region when it opened in 2022): most items around 300 yen, with homeware, storage, travel bags and small gifts. First shop on the walk north from lunch.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:25pm, a 6-7 min walk north from Ginza Tamai

Name: MUJI Ginza (flagship)
Description: MUJI's global flagship: clothing, stationery, homeware and a large food floor over several levels, with a bakery on 1F. Recent visitors report the tax-free counter is on 4F.
Best Time To Visit: ~12:50pm, 2-3 min from 3COINS+plus

Name: UNIQLO TOKYO (flagship)
Neighborhood: Ginza 3-chome, Marronnier Gate Ginza 2 (1F-4F), across the street from MUJI Ginza
Description: UNIQLO flagship over four floors, with the full range and a custom-print corner. GU is on 5F of the same building and Daiso on 6F.
Best Time To Visit: ~1:35pm, across the street from MUJI Ginza
Tags: UNIQLO; flagship; everyday clothing; tax-free; Ginza

Name: Cross Shinjuku Vision (3D cat screen)
Description: The giant 3D calico cat on the curved rooftop screen facing the East Exit plaza. The cat appears between adverts, so allow about 10 minutes. Best after dark. A few minutes on foot from the Don Quijote in Kabuki-cho.
Best Time To Visit: After dinner - about 15 min from Tokyo Station on the JR Chuo Line rapid. No closing time to beat

Name: Tori no Ichi Ueno Honten (鳥乃壱 上野本店)
Neighborhood: Higashi-Ueno, about 5 min walk from JR Ueno Station
Hours: Sat-Sun 16:00-23:00; weekday lunch 11:00-15:00 and dinner from 16:00 (17:00 Tue) to 23:00
Description: DAY 11 DINNER. Large yakitori restaurant (130 seats) with more than skewers: chicken hot pot, clay-pot rice (kamameshi), fried chicken and chawanmushi. Tabelog 3.40 (302 reviews) - under your usual 3.5 line, chosen from the walk-in-friendly options after Yuwaeru and Renkon were fully booked. Ordering is by QR code on your phone. Smoking is separated. Google reviews mention a table charge of about 490 yen per person and are mixed on service.
Best Time To Visit: ~8:15pm (Sun Oct 11), after JINS at Atre Ueno - open until 11:00pm
Tags: dinner; yakitori; chicken hot pot; kamameshi; Ueno
Reservation Info: Not booked - online booking via Tabelog. With 130 seats a walk-in is realistic, but it is the Sunday of a holiday weekend

Name: Asakusa Gyukatsu (beef cutlet)
